And Lamech was old and advanced in years, and his eyes were dim that he could not see, and Tubal Cain, his son, was leading him and it was one day that Lamech went into the field and Tubal Cain his son was with him, and whilst they were walking in the field, Cain the son of Adam advanced towards them; for Lamech was very old and could not see much, and Tubal Cain his son was very young.
And Tubal Cain told his father to draw his bow, and with the arrows he smote Cain, who was yet far off, and he slew him, for he appeared to them to be an animal.
And the arrows entered Cain’s body although he was distant from them, and he fell to the ground and died.
And YAHUAH requited Cain’s evil according to his wickedness, which he had done to his brother Abel, according to the word of YAHUAH which he had spoken.
And it came to pass when Cain had died, that Lamech and Tubal went to see the animal which they had slain, and they saw, and behold Cain their grandfather was fallen dead upon the earth.
And Lamech was very much grieved at having done this, and in clapping his hands together he struck his son and caused his death.
And the wives of Lamech heard what Lamech had done, and they sought to kill him.
And the wives of Lamech hated him from that day, because he slew Cain and Tubal Cain, and the wives of Lamech separated from him, and would not hearken to him in those days.
And Lamech came to his wives, and he pressed them to listen to him about this matter.

And he said to his wives Adah and Zillah, Hear my voice O wives of Lamech, attend to my words, for now you have imagined and said that I slew a man with my wounds, and a child with my stripes for their having done no violence, but surely know that I am old and grey-headed, and that my eyes are heavy through age, and I did this thing unknowingly.

And the wives of Lamech listened to him in this matter, and they returned to him with the advice of their father Adam, but they bore no children to him from that time, knowing that Elohim’s anger was increasing in those days against the sons of men, to destroy them with the waters of the flood for their evil doings.

And Mahlallel the son of Cainan lived sixty-five years and he begat Jared; and Jared lived sixty-two years and he begat Enoch. « • • • Mainstream readings of Genesis 4:26 take the phrase “then began men to call upon the name of YAHUAH” as a moment of spiritual awakening. Jasher — along with the rabbinic tradition behind it — takes the opposite view. In the days of Enosh, the sons of men began to “call upon” YAHUAH’s name in a very specific, very idolatrous way: they began to name their carved images after Him. This is the origin of idolatry inside the covenant line. Not the worship of other gods invented from scratch, but the fashioning of images of wood and stone and calling those images by the name of the true one. This is what the institutional church has done with the Messiah for two thousand years under a different name. This is what some elements of Hebrew roots are now doing with the Father under a different name. It is not new. It is the oldest deception there is, and it started in the fifth generation from Adam. The river Gihon flood is not in Genesis, but it is not contradicted by Genesis either. Jasher preserves a memory that before the great flood of Noah, YAHUAH gave the earth a warning judgment — one-third of the earth drowned under a local flood, as a mercy intended to wake the rest up. It did not work. Jasher verse 6 is one of the bleakest lines in all of apocryphal literature: “notwithstanding this, the sons of men did not turn from their evil ways, and their hands were yet extended to do evil in the sight of YAHUAH.” This sets the pattern. YAHUAH never drops the hammer without warning first. He sent Gihon before He sent the global flood. He sent the prophets before He sent Babylon. He sent John the Baptist before He sent the Messiah. He is sending today’s awakening to the remnant before He sends what the book of Revelation calls the hour of trial. The mercy precedes the sentence every time. And every time, some refuse to hear. Jasher chapter 2 verse 20 is a line that should stop the modern Christian and modern Torah observant reader in their tracks. In the generation before the flood, “some of the sons of men caused their wives to drink a draught that would render them barren, in order that they might retain their figures and by which their beautiful appearance might not fade.” Abortion is not a modern invention. Sterilization-for-vanity is not a modern invention. Using contraception to preserve a lifestyle of indulgence rather than to raise a godly seed is not a modern invention. Jasher names this sin in the pre-flood generation as one of the practices that provoked YAHUAH. The fruitful-and-multiply command given in Genesis 1:28 was not a suggestion. It was the first command ever given to humanity. The couples in the days of Enosh refused the first command YAHUAH ever gave — and Jasher includes it in the list of reasons the anger of YAHUAH was provoked. The awakening remnant has to reckon with this honestly. The modern assumption that the family is a lifestyle choice rather than a covenantal calling has its roots in Cainite soil. The death of Cain is a strange, almost comic moment — an elderly blind Lamech being led by his young son Tubal-Cain into a hunting accident that kills the first murderer of human history. But Jasher verse 29 is the point: “And YAHUAH requited Cain’s evil according to his wickedness.” The original sentence on Cain in Genesis 4:15 — whoever kills Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold — is satisfied by Lamech’s own sevenfold confession to his wives later. The sovereign hand of YAHUAH reached across generations to bring Cain’s murder back to his own head. No sin gets lost in the shuffle. No spilled blood goes unaccounted for. The God who remembered Abel seven generations later is the same God who remembers every drop of martyr blood shed in every century from then until now. “Vengeance is mine, I will repay” (Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19). He means it literally. He has proved it from the beginning. Enosh-generation corruption and the two-front fall One more thing must be said about the Enosh generation before we leave it, and it requires reading Jasher alongside the Book of Enoch. Jasher 2 gives us the terrestrial half of a two-front corruption. The Book of Enoch gives us the celestial half. They are not two separate accounts. They are the same catastrophe seen from two angles — the earthly symptom Jasher describes, and the heavenly cause Enoch names. Jasher 2:4 says the sons of men made images of brass and iron, wood and stone, and they called those images by the name of Yahuah (God). The Book of Enoch tells us who was standing behind the culture that taught them how. In 1 Enoch 8:1–3 we are told that Azâzêl taught men the making of swords and knives, the working of metals, the use of cosmetic stones and colored tinctures, while Semjâzâ taught enchantments and root-cutting, and Baraqîjâl taught astrology, and Kôkabêl taught the constellations, and Araqiêl taught the signs of the earth, and Shamsiêl taught the signs of the sun, and Sariêl taught the course of the moon. The idols of Jasher 2 were not fashioned by imagination alone. The metallurgy that made the brass and iron idols was taught. The colored tinctures that glazed them were taught. The astrological meanings that were assigned to each image were taught. The first image-cult of humanity was not a naive craft project. It was a curriculum — and the teachers were the fallen sons of the heaven, the Watchers of Mount Hermon, who would come down in the days of Jared and begin the formal instruction that Jasher records only as its visible effect. "And these are the names of their leaders. Semjâzâ, who was their leader, said to them: 'I fear you will not indeed agree to do this deed, and I alone shall have to pay the penalty of a great sin.' And they all answered him and said: 'Let us all swear an oath, and all bind ourselves by mutual curses not to abandon this plan but to do this thing.' Then swore they all together and bound themselves by mutual curses upon it. And they were in all two hundred; who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon" — 1 Enoch 6:3–6. That oath on Hermon is the hinge between Jasher's half of the story and Enoch's. Jasher shows the Enosh-generation effect. Enoch shows the Jared-generation cause. Read the two together and the pre-flood world comes into focus as a single collapse — a collapse the institutional church covered up when it took Enoch out of its canons, and a collapse the Hebrew Roots community often sees only in the spectacle of giants and not in the quieter corruption of the image and the tongue. The sterility draughts of Jasher 2:20 are part of the same curriculum. The text says some of the sons of men caused their wives to drink a draught to render them barren so they might retain their figures. In 1 Enoch 7:1 the Watchers are described as teaching their wives "charms and enchantments, and the cutting of roots, and made them acquainted with plants." Root-cutting is botanical pharmacology. The enchantment that accompanied it was the sacramental framing that made the drug feel religious. The pre-flood generation did not abort and sterilize with mere chemicals; they abolished the fruitful-and-multiply command with a ritual. The chemical was the mechanism. The ritual was the permission. "Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth" (Genesis 1:28), the first command ever given to humanity, was refused by a people who preferred the look of their own bodies to the seed of their own line. The command came from Elohim (God). The permission to refuse it came from the Watchers. Every modern regime that asks a woman to destroy her womb's fruit in exchange for a career, a figure, a freedom, a relief, an economic future, is operating on permission that was first written on the summit of Hermon. Naming this honestly does not indict the women who have been caught by that regime. It names the teachers who wrote the permission. The victims of this catechism are many — and the Father heals them. Psalm 127:3 still stands: "Lo, children are a heritage of Yahuah (the Lord): and the fruit of the womb is his reward." The womb itself still belongs to the Maker. The draught, the pill, the scalpel, the counselor who normalized the choice, and the system that built the clinics — all of them ultimately trace back through human generations to Hermon. The gentleness of the Father has been calling daughters out of that whole architecture for centuries, and He is still calling. The river Gihon flood in Jasher 2:6 is the warning-flood before the global flood. Yahuah (God) drowned one-third of the earth before He drowned all of it, as a mercy intended to wake the rest up. The two-front corruption did not stop for the warning. The image-cults continued. The sterility-cults continued. The teaching of the Watchers had gone too deep, and the only instrument strong enough to cleanse the earth of the full spread of it was the global flood itself. The warnings of our own age may look different — a pandemic, a war, a collapse, a judgment on a specific industry — but the pattern is fixed. Yahuah (God) warns before He strikes, and strikes when the warnings are ignored. Jasher and Enoch together tell us that the Father is always more merciful than we guess, and the final sentence always falls only after a long patience. "The Master is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance" (2 Peter 3:9). That verse is not a contradiction of the flood. That verse is the flood explained. He waited one hundred and twenty years. He is waiting now. He will not wait forever. The retribution on Cain in Jasher 2:29 — Lamech's arrow striking the first murderer sevenfold generations later — tells us the ledger was being kept all along. No sin was lost. No shed blood was forgotten. The book of Jude picks up this pre-flood ledger in the same breath it picks up Enoch (Jude 1:14–15). The Watchers reserved in chains of darkness unto the judgment of the great day are in the ledger. The children of the Watchers slain in the first purge are in the ledger. Cain's blood-debt requited on Cain's own head is in the ledger. The awakening remnant lives now inside a ledger that has been kept from Adam. The sons of Adam walk under a mercy that has been patient from Adam. And when the Father closes the book and opens the other books, every line of it will have been written perfectly (Revelation 20:12). Cross-references: Genesis 4:17–26; Genesis 5:1–32; Genesis 1:28; Deuteronomy 32:35; Romans 12:19; Psalm 115:4–8; Isaiah 44:9–20; Jeremiah 10:1–16; Hebrews 11:5; Jude 1:14–15; Revelation 9:20–21; 2 Timothy 3:1–5; 1 Enoch 6:1–6; 1 Enoch 7:1–6; 1 Enoch 8:1–3; Psalm 127:3; 2 Peter 3:9; Revelation 20:12; Deuteronomy 4:15–20; Jude 1:14–15.

chapters.title: Enoch Reigns and Ascends — The First Prophet-King

verses.text: And Enoch lived sixty-five years and he begat Methuselah; and Enoch walked with Elohim (God) after having begot Methuselah, and he served YAHUAH (the Lord), and despised the evil ways of men.
And the soul of Enoch was wrapped up in the instruction of YAHUAH, in knowledge and in understanding; and he wisely retired from the sons of men, and secreted himself from them for many days.
And it was at the expiration of many years, whilst he was serving YAHUAH, and praying before him in his house, that an angel of YAHUAH called to him from Heaven, and he said, Here am I.

And he said, Rise, go forth from your house and from the place where you dost hide thyself, and appear to the sons of men, in order that you may teach them the way in which they should go and the work which they must accomplish to enter in the ways of Elohim.

And Enoch rose up according to the word of YAHUAH, and went forth from his house, from his place and from the chamber in which he was concealed; and he went to the sons of men and taught them the ways of YAHUAH, and at that time assembled the sons of men and acquainted them with the instruction of YAHUAH.
And he ordered it to be proclaimed in all places where the sons of men dwelt, saying, Where is the man who wishes to know the ways of YAHUAH and good works? let him come to Enoch.

And all the sons of men then assembled to him, for all who desired this thing went to Enoch, and Enoch reigned over the sons of men according to the word of YAHUAH, and they came and bowed to him and they heard his word.
And the spirit of Elohim was upon Enoch, and he taught all his men the wisdom of Elohim and his ways, and the sons of men served YAHUAH all the days of Enoch, and they came to hear his wisdom.

And all the kings of the sons of men, both first and last, together with their princes and judges, came to Enoch when they heard of his wisdom, and they bowed down to him, and they also required of Enoch to reign over them, to which he consented.
And they assembled in all, one hundred and thirty kings and princes, and they made Enoch king over them and they were all under his power and command.
And Enoch taught them wisdom, knowledge, and the ways of YAHUAH; and he made peace amongst them, and peace was throughout the earth during the life of Enoch.
And Enoch reigned over the sons of men two hundred and forty-three years, and he did justice and righteousness with all his people, and he led them in the ways of YAHUAH.
And these are the generations of Enoch, Methuselah, Elisha, and Elimelech, three sons; and their sisters were Melca and Nahmah, and Methuselah lived eighty-seven years and he begat Lamech.

And it was in the fifty-sixth year of the life of Lamech when Adam died; nine hundred and thirty years old was he at his death, and his two sons, with Enoch and Methuselah his son, buried him with great pomp, as at the burial of kings, in the cave which Elohim had told him.
And in that place all the sons of men made a great mourning and weeping on account of Adam; it has therefore become a custom among the sons of men to this day.
And Adam died because he ate of the tree of knowledge; he and his children after him, as YAHUAH Elohim (the Lord God) had spoken.

And it was in the year of Adam’s death which was the two hundred and forty-third year of the reign of Enoch, in that time Enoch resolved to separate himself from the sons of men and to secret himself as at first in order to serve YAHUAH.
And Enoch did so, but did not entirely secret himself from them, but kept away from the sons of men three days and then went to them for one day.

And during the three days that he was in his chamber, he prayed to, and praised YAHUAH his Elohim, and the day on which he went and appeared to his subjects he taught them the ways of YAHUAH, and all they asked him about YAHUAH he told them.

And he did in this manner for many years, and he afterward concealed himself for six days, and appeared to his people one day in seven; and after that once in a month, and then once in a year, until all the kings, princes and sons of men sought for him, and desired again to see the face of Enoch, and to hear his word; but they could not, as all the sons of men were greatly afraid of Enoch, and they feared to approach him on account of the Godlike awe that was seated upon his countenance; therefore no man could look at him, fearing he might be punished and die.

And all the kings and princes resolved to assemble the sons of men, and to come to Enoch, thinking that they might all speak to him at the time when he should come forth amongst them, and they did so.

And the day came when Enoch went forth and they all assembled and came to him, and Enoch spoke to them the words of YAHUAH and he taught them wisdom and knowledge, and they bowed down before him and they said, May the king live! May the king live!

And in some time after, when the kings and princes and the sons of men were speaking to Enoch, and Enoch was teaching them the ways of Elohim, behold an angel of YAHUAH then called to Enoch from heaven, and wished to bring him up to heaven to make him reign there over the sons of Elohim, as he had reigned over the sons of men upon earth.

When at that time Enoch heard this he went and assembled all the inhabitants of the earth, and taught them wisdom and knowledge and gave them divine instructions, and he said to them, I have been required to ascend into heaven, I therefore do not know the day of my going.
And now therefore I will teach you wisdom and knowledge and will give you instruction before I leave you, how to act upon earth by which you may live; and he did so.

And he taught them wisdom and knowledge, and gave them instruction, and he reproved them, and he placed before them statutes and judgments to do upon earth, and he made peace amongst them, and he taught them everlasting life, and dwelt with them some time teaching them all these things.

And at that time the sons of men were with Enoch, and Enoch was speaking to them, and they lifted up their eyes and the likeness of a great horse descended from heaven, and the horse paced in the air;
And they told Enoch what they had seen, and Enoch said to them, On my account does this horse descend upon earth; the time is come when I must go from you and I shall no more be seen by you.
And the horse descended at that time and stood before Enoch, and all the sons of men that were with Enoch saw him.

And Enoch then again ordered a voice to be proclaimed, saying, Where is the man who delights to know the ways of YAHUAH his Elohim (the Lord his God), let him come this day to Enoch before he is taken from us.

And all the sons of men assembled and came to Enoch that day; and all the kings of the earth with their princes and counsellors remained with him that day; and Enoch then taught the sons of men wisdom and knowledge, and gave them divine instruction; and he bade them serve YAHUAH and walk in his ways all the days of their lives, and he continued to make peace amongst them.
And it was after this that he rose up and rode upon the horse; and he went forth and all the sons of men went after him, about eight hundred thousand men; and they went with him one day’s journey.

And the second day he said to them, Return home to your tents, why will you go? perhaps you may die; and some of them went from him, and those that remained went with him six day’s journey; and Enoch said to them every day, Return to your tents, lest you may die; but they were not willing to return, and they went with him.
And on the sixth day some of the men remained and clung to him, and they said to him, We will go with you to the place where you go; as YAHUAH lives, death only shall separate us.
And they urged so much to go with him, that he ceased speaking to them; and they went after him and would not return;

And when the kings returned they caused a census to be taken, in order to know the number of remaining men that went with Enoch; and it was upon the seventh day that Enoch ascended into heaven in a whirlwind, with horses and chariots of fire.
And on the eighth day all the kings that had been with Enoch sent to bring back the number of men that were with Enoch, in that place from which he ascended into heaven.

And all those kings went to the place and they found the earth there filled with snow, and upon the snow were large stones of snow, and one said to the other, Come, let us break through the snow and see, perhaps the men that remained with Enoch are dead, and are now under the stones of snow, and they searched but could not find him, for he had ascended into heaven. « • • • Jasher’s account of Enoch is both more and less than what the Book of Enoch itself gives us. Less, because Jasher does not open the cosmic scope of the Ethiopic Enoch — no Watchers, no journeys through Sheol, no tour of the firmaments. More, because Jasher shows Enoch as a reigning prophet-king, a man who ruled 130 kings and princes from his hidden chamber and who, seven days before his ascension, held a final teaching session the way a father holds a final blessing over his children. Enoch is the prototype of every covenant teacher who will come after him: hidden for long seasons to be alone with YAHUAH, then released to feed the flock, then hidden again. The detail that “no man could look at him, fearing he might be punished and die” is a detail that matches Moses (Exodus 34:29–35), matches Elijah, and matches the transfigured Messiah (Matthew 17:2). The glory of YAHUAH rests on those who have been long alone with Him. Mankind’s natural reaction to unveiled glory is not attraction — it is fear. That is worth sitting with, because there are many today who claim intimate knowledge of the divine but whose presence provokes no reverence in anyone. The counterfeit glories of the age can be recognized by what they do not produce. The genuine article drives people to their faces (Isaiah 6:5). The chariot-and-horse ascension in a whirlwind matches Elijah’s ascension (2 Kings 2:11) so precisely that it is impossible to miss the typological weight. There are two men in the Tanakh who did not taste death — Enoch and Elijah — and Jasher aligns their departures in the same mode of transport. Scripture teaches that what is begun in the first man of a type is completed in the last. And in Revelation 11:3–12 we meet “two witnesses” at the end of days, whose ministries parallel Elijah (stopping rain, calling down fire) and Enoch (prophesying judgment — Jude quoting Enoch). The early pattern prefigures the last-days pattern. The chariot that took Enoch, and the whirlwind that took Elijah, will very likely come for them again. Notice what Enoch did not do. He did not build a temple. He did not found a religion. He did not inaugurate a priesthood. He taught “the ways of YAHUAH” — which in a pre-Sinai world can only mean the basic moral and ceremonial knowledge that had been preserved from Adam and Seth. The commandments of YAHUAH were not unknown before Sinai. They were oral before they were written. Enoch taught them. Noah obeyed the distinction of clean and unclean animals before the flood (Genesis 7:2). Abraham kept YAHUAH’s commandments and statutes and laws (Genesis 26:5). The idea that Torah was a late invention imposed on an innocent world is a lie the institutional church tells when it needs to justify its own rejection of Torah. Jasher and Genesis both say the opposite. Torah was always in force; Sinai was the public written covenant declaration of what had been known and preserved since Eden. Enoch the witness — the Jasher portrait under the Enochian office Jasher's portrait of Enoch is compressed. The Book of Enoch expands it. Read side by side, the two books tell one story — and the office they describe is the office of the witness, not the witnessed. This distinction is the single most important guard against the error the institutional church committed when it stripped Enoch from its canons, and against the mirror-image error R.H. Charles committed when he assumed the phrase son of man was a title reserved for Messiah (Christ) alone and rewrote passages that did not fit his assumption. Enoch is a son of Adam. He is a finger pointing. He is not the one pointed at. Jasher confirms this in every line Jasher gives us about him, and the Book of Enoch confirms it across one hundred and eight chapters. Enoch's office is the office of John the Baptist in prototype. Both were appointed before they were conceived — Enoch walked with Elohim (God) three hundred years because the grain was clean before he was ever born, and John was filled with the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) from his mother's womb. Both were set apart from the general population by their manner of life — Enoch hidden for long seasons and released in the final days to feed the people, John in the wilderness with a leather belt and locusts and wild honey. Both had one message: the one who is greater is coming, and I am not him. Enoch's message is compressed in the line Jude quotes: "Behold, Yahuah (the Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints, to execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him" (Jude 1:14–15). John's was: "There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose" (Mark 1:7). Two men, two ages, one office. The witness names the coming, steps aside, and lets the Elohim (God) the witness saw be the one the world beholds. The detail Jasher gives — that Enoch taught a hundred and thirty kings and princes in his hidden chamber, and that peace was throughout the earth during his life — tells us something about what was happening in the world at the same time the Watchers were beginning their descent. Two kingship architectures were competing for the pre-flood earth. The Watcher architecture was attempting to seize the nations from above, through taught enchantments and taught warfare and taught cosmetic glamour and taught astrology. The Adamic architecture, preserved from Seth through Enosh through Kenan through Mahalalel through Jared through Enoch, was holding the thread from below — a covenant line with a reigning prophet-king at its head, teaching the kings of the earth the ways of Yahuah (God). For three hundred years, Enoch's kingship of the line held the Watchers back. When Enoch was translated and Methuselah inherited the office, and when Methuselah was old, the pressure finally broke through. The flood came after Enoch's generation not because Enoch failed but because the kingship that Enoch had exercised was no longer walking the earth, and the line had narrowed to Noah alone. The Book of Enoch expands the vision Jasher only hints at. In 1 Enoch 14 the man Enoch sees the throne of glory — "And I looked and saw a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon. And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow" (1 Enoch 14:18–20). The one Enoch sees on the throne is the Ancient of Days — the Formed of the Formless, the Expressed Word through whom and by whom and for whom all things were made, who would in the fullness of time walk on the Galilean hills as Yahusha (Jesus). This is the same one whom Daniel saw: "I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire" (Daniel 7:9). This is the same one whom John saw: "His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow; and his eyes were as a flame of fire" (Revelation 1:14). Enoch saw him first. Daniel saw him. John saw him. The one seen by all three is the one who walked in the flesh as Yahusha (Jesus), the Elohim (God) who has a Father — and the Father is not another Elohim (God) in a pantheon, because the Father is the Formless from whom the Formed proceeds, beyond the category being. The Shema holds: "Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah (the Lord) our Elohim (God) is one Yahuah (Lord)" (Deuteronomy 6:4). One Elohim (God) in two modes — Formless and Formed — and the Son alone makes the Formless known (John 1:18). When Jasher 3 tells us that no man could look at Enoch without fearing that he might be punished and die, the text is describing the residue of that throne-room vision on a man's face. The same residue was on Moses after forty days on Sinai (Exodus 34:29–30), and on the three disciples after seeing Yahusha (Jesus) transfigured (Matthew 17:6). Enoch's kingship was not a ruling from a palace. It was a reigning from the mountain of vision. He had been long alone with the Ancient of Days, and the Ancient of Days had sent him back to teach the earth for a season before taking him home. The horse and chariot in a whirlwind at the end of his life matches Elijah's departure exactly (2 Kings 2:11), and the two-witnesses passage of Revelation 11 describes two men in the last days who prophesy for 1,260 days, have power over rain and fire and plague, are killed in the street of the great city, lie unburied for three and a half days, and are raised and translated upward in a cloud — the two men most readily identified in the text are Enoch and Elijah, the two men in Tanakh who did not taste death, coming back at the end of the age to finish the witness they began. If Jasher and 1 Enoch are right about who Enoch was, Revelation 11 is right about where Enoch will be seen again. The office of the witness did not close when he was translated the first time. It was held open for the final hour. A line must be drawn here that the voice of this commentary will not cross. Enoch saw the throne. He did not sit on it. When 1 Enoch 71 records the Head of Days saying to Enoch "You are the son of man who was born unto righteousness," the phrase is a son-of-Adam designation — confirmation that Enoch is of the covenant lineage, a righteous human in the seed war, the clearest pre-flood demonstration of what election produces in an Adamic man. It is not an enthronement. It is not a transfer of the messianic office. Enoch sees the Elect One; he is not the Elect One. The Elect One was named before the sun and stars were created (1 Enoch 48:2–3). Enoch was named by his father Jared at birth. These are not the same figure, and the Parables themselves establish the distinction across thirty-five chapters before the son-of-man address arrives. The correct reading does not collapse the distinction at the last moment. It honors it. R.H. Charles missed this. The institutional church missed it by omitting the book. The awakening reader who is now meeting Enoch for the first time must not miss it either. Charles's error — making son of man a messianic title — produced his rewrite of the Ethiopic. The reverse error — accepting the son-of-man identification as messianic and thereby enthroning Enoch — would produce a book that turns the greatest witness into the one witnessed. Our commentary honors the witness. It worships the one the witness saw. And where is Enoch now? Jasher says he went up in a whirlwind with horses and chariots of fire. The Book of Enoch says he was shown the dwelling of the Elect One among the trees that do not lose their foliage, in the garden on the mountain — the garden the Watchers had tried to corrupt the earth away from, the garden still preserved for the righteous. Enoch dwells in Eden to this day. Not on a throne. In the garden, with the first fathers, as a son of Adam in his appointed place. When the final trumpet sounds and the witnesses are released for their last testimony, the garden will open and the office of the witness will walk out of it. Until then, the same office is walking in the awakening remnant — a people not on a throne, not building a kingdom, but pointing at the one who is coming. We are not the Messiah (Christ). We are only the finger. The hand is his. Cross-references: Genesis 5:21–24; Hebrews 11:5; Jude 1:14–15; 2 Kings 2:11; Exodus 34:29–35; Matthew 17:1–8; Revelation 11:3–12; Isaiah 6:1–5; Malachi 4:5–6; Genesis 26:5; Genesis 7:2; 1 Enoch 1:2; 1 Enoch 14:18–22; 1 Enoch 48:2–3; 1 Enoch 71:14–17; Daniel 7:9; Revelation 1:13–18; Revelation 11:3–12; Deuteronomy 6:4; John 1:18; Luke 1:13–17; Mark 1:7; Exodus 34:29–30; Matthew 17:1–8.

chapters.title: Methuselah, the Return of Corruption, and the Birth of Noah

verses.text: And all the days that Enoch lived upon earth, were three hundred and sixty-five years.
And when Enoch had ascended into heaven, all the kings of the earth rose and took Methuselah his son and anointed him, and they caused him to reign over them in the place of his father.

And Methuselah acted uprightly in the sight of Elohim (God), as his father Enoch had taught him, and he likewise during the whole of his life taught the sons of men wisdom, knowledge and the fear of Elohim, and he did not turn from the good way either to the right or to the left.

But in the latter days of Methuselah, the sons of men turned from YAHUAH (the Lord), they corrupted the earth, they robbed and plundered each other, and they rebelled against Elohim and they transgressed, and they corrupted their ways, and would not hearken to the voice of Methuselah, but rebelled against him.
And YAHUAH was exceedingly wroth against them, and YAHUAH continued to destroy the seed in those days, so that there was neither sowing nor reaping in the earth.
For when they sowed the ground in order that they might obtain food for their support, behold, thorns and thistles were produced which they did not sow.

And still the sons of men did not turn from their evil ways, and their hands were still extended to do evil in the sight of Elohim, and they provoked YAHUAH with their evil ways, and YAHUAH was very wroth, and repented that he had made man.
And he thought to destroy and annihilate them and he did so.
In those days when Lamech the son of Methuselah was one hundred and sixty years old, Seth the son of Adam died.
And all the days that Seth lived, were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died.
And Lamech was one hundred and eighty years old when he took Ashmua, the daughter of Elishaa the son of Enoch his uncle, and she conceived.
And at that time the sons of men sowed the ground, and a little food was produced, yet the sons of men did not turn from their evil ways, and they trespassed and rebelled against Elohim.
And the wife of Lamech conceived and bare him a son at that time, at the revolution of the year.

And Methuselah called his name Noah, saying, The earth was in his days at rest and free from corruption, and Lamech his father called his name Menachem, saying, This one shall comfort us in our works and miserable toil in the earth, which Elohim had cursed.
And the child grew up and was weaned, and he went in the ways of his father Methuselah, perfect and upright with Elohim.

And all the sons of men departed from the ways of YAHUAH in those days as they multiplied upon the face of the earth with sons and daughters, and they taught one another their evil practices and they continued sinning against YAHUAH.
And every man made to himself a god, and they robbed and plundered every man his neighbor as well as his relative, and they corrupted the earth, and the earth was filled with violence.

And their judges and rulers went to the daughters of men and took their wives by force from their husbands according to their choice, and the sons of men in those days took from the cattle of the earth, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air, and taught the mixture of animals of one species with the other, in order therewith to provoke YAHUAH; and Elohim saw the whole earth and it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted its ways upon earth, all men and all animals.

And YAHUAH said, I will blot out man that I created from the face of the earth, yea from man to the birds of the air, together with cattle and beasts that are in the field for I repent that I made them.

And all men who walked in the ways of YAHUAH, died in those days, before YAHUAH brought the evil upon man which he had declared, for this was from YAHUAH, that they should not see the evil which YAHUAH spoke of concerning the sons of men.

And Noah found grace in the sight of YAHUAH, and YAHUAH chose him and his children to raise up seed from them upon the face of the whole earth. « • • • Jasher’s description of pre-flood corruption is more detailed than Genesis 6 and should be read alongside what the Book of Enoch describes in 1 Enoch 6–8. Enoch names the Watchers — two hundred angels who fell by coordinated oath on Mount Hermon — as the direct cause of the spread of occult knowledge and forbidden mixture. Jasher, written much later and preserved through a different stream, names the results of that fall without dwelling on the fallen angels themselves. The robbing and plundering, the taking of wives by force, and — most striking — the mixture of animals of one species with the other to “provoke YAHUAH” are all consequences of the Watcher-taught knowledge that Enoch describes. The mixture of species is not a minor detail. The command of Leviticus 19:19 — “You shall not let your cattle gender with a diverse kind” — was given at Sinai and is almost always dismissed by modern readers as a quaint agricultural rule. Jasher tells us what the rule is actually about. The pre-flood generation deliberately crossed species “in order to provoke YAHUAH.” They were not experimenting with animal husbandry. They were striking at the created order. They were telling the Creator that His distinctions were not going to stand. Leviticus 19:19, read in the light of Jasher 4:18, is not quaint. It is YAHUAH’s covenant refusal to let the sin of the pre-flood world return under His name. Every one of His commandments is of this character: what looks small is load-bearing, and behind every small command is a memory of the catastrophe that made the command necessary. The awakening remnant should be sober about what is happening in the earth right now. The re-mixture of species, the editing of the genome, the normalization of chimeras — the pre-flood practice is being recapitulated in front of us. YAHUSHA said that the last days would be as the days of Noah (Matthew 24:37–39). He did not say that as metaphor. He said it as pattern. The same Creator who flooded the earth over this will judge again. Noah’s name is given twice in Jasher verse 14 — Noah by Methuselah, meaning the earth will find rest; Menachem by Lamech, meaning this one will comfort us. Both names are true. Both are messianic in the pattern they prefigure. Noah is the one who carries the seed through the judgment. The Messiah is the one who carries the seed through the final judgment. Both are named comforters in advance. “Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God” (Isaiah 40:1) — the comfort of the last days is a comfort that comes through an ark. And notice — Noah found grace (Jasher 4:21, Genesis 6:8) before the flood was sent, not because he had earned his way out of judgment but because YAHUAH had chosen him. The language is covenantal. “YAHUAH chose him and his children to raise up seed from them.” This is the first explicit election statement in scripture after the garden. It is the bridge between Adam (the one who lost the garden) and Abraham (the one called out to begin its restoration). The whole line between Adam and Abraham is a line of chosen ones. The Hebrew roots reader who has imbibed the “inclusion gospel” — the idea that any sincere Torah-keeper is thereby counted as chosen Israel — has to reckon honestly with how this works. YAHUAH does the choosing. He chose Seth over Cain. He chose Noah over the rest of his generation. He chose Shem over Ham and Japheth. He chose Abraham over the other sons of Terah. Every stage of the narrative narrows the seed. It does not broaden to include whoever decides to identify with it. Cross-references: Genesis 6:1–13; 1 Enoch 6:1–8:4; Leviticus 19:19; Matthew 24:37–39; Luke 17:26–27; 1 Peter 3:20; 2 Peter 2:4–5; Isaiah 40:1; Genesis 5:28–29; Hebrews 11:7.

chapters.title: The Hundred and Twenty Years, and the Ark Begun

verses.text: And it was in the eighty-fourth year of the life of Noah, that Enoch the son of Seth died, he was nine hundred and five years old at his death.
And in the one hundred and seventy ninth year of the life of Noah, Cainan the son of Enosh died, and all the days of Cainan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died.
And in the two hundred and thirty fourth year of the life of Noah, Mahlallel the son of Cainan died, and the days of Mahlallel were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died.
And Jared the son of Mahlallel died in those days, in the three hundred and thirty-sixth year of the life of Noah; and all the days of Jared were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died.
And all who followed YAHUAH (the Lord) died in those days, before they saw the evil which Elohim (God) declared to do upon earth.

And after the lapse of many years, in the four hundred and eightieth year of the life of Noah, when all those men, who followed YAHUAH had died away from amongst the sons of men, and only Methuselah was then left, Elohim said to Noah and Methuselah, saying,

Speak you, and proclaim to the sons of men, saying, Thus says YAHUAH, return from your evil ways and forsake your works, and YAHUAH will repent of the evil that he declared to do to you, so that it shall not come to pass.

For thus says YAHUAH, Behold I give you a period of one hundred and twenty years; if you will turn to me and forsake your evil ways, then will I also turn away from the evil which I told you, and it shall not exist, says YAHUAH.
And Noah and Methuselah spoke all the words of YAHUAH to the sons of men, day after day, constantly speaking to them.
But the sons of men would not hearken to them, nor incline their ears to their words, and they were stiffnecked.
And YAHUAH granted them a period of one hundred and twenty years, saying, If they will return, then will Elohim repent of the evil, so as not to destroy the earth.
Noah the son of Lamech refrained from taking a wife in those days, to beget children, for he said, Surely now Elohim will destroy the earth, therefore then shall I beget children?
And Noah was a just man, he was perfect in his generation, and YAHUAH chose him to raise up seed from his seed upon the face of the earth.
And YAHUAH said to Noah, Take to you a wife, and beget children, for I have seen you righteous before me in this generation.

And you shall raise up seed, and your children with you, in the midst of the earth; and Noah went and took a wife, and he chose Naamah the daughter of Enoch, and she was five hundred and eighty years old.
And Noah was four hundred and ninety-eight years old, when he took Naamah for a wife.

And Naamah conceived and bare a son, and he called his name Japheth, saying, Elohim has enlarged me in the earth; and she conceived again and bare a son, and he called his name Shem, saying, Elohim has made me a remnant, to raise up seed in the midst of the earth.
And Noah was five hundred and two years old when Naamah bare Shem, and the boys grew up and went in the ways of YAHUAH, in all that Methuselah and Noah their father taught them.
And Lamech the father of Noah, died in those days; yet verily he did not go with all his heart in the ways of his father, and he died in the hundred and ninety-fifth year of the life of Noah.
And all the days of Lamech were seven hundred and seventy years, and he died.

And all the sons of men who knew YAHUAH, died in that year before YAHUAH brought evil upon them; for YAHUAH willed them to die, so as not to behold the evil that Elohim would bring upon their brothers and relatives, as he had so declared to do.

In that time, YAHUAH said to Noah and Methuselah, Stand forth and proclaim to the sons of men all the words that I spoke to you in those days, peradventure they may turn from their evil ways, and I will then repent of the evil and will not bring it.
And Noah and Methuselah stood forth, and said in the ears of the sons of men, all that Elohim had spoken concerning them.
But the sons of men would not hearken, neither would they incline their ears to all their declarations.
And it was after this that YAHUAH said to Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me, on account of their evil deeds, and behold I will destroy the earth.
And do you take to you gopher wood, and go to a certain place and make a large ark, and place it in that spot.
And thus shall you make it; three hundred cubits its length, fifty cubits broad and thirty cubits high.
And you shall make to you a door, open at its side, and to a cubit you shall finish above, and cover it within and without with pitch.
And behold I will bring the flood of waters upon the earth, and all flesh be destroyed, from under the heavens all that is upon earth shall perish.
And you and your household shall go and gather two couple of all living things, male and female, and shall bring them to the ark, to raise up seed from them upon earth.
And gather to you all food that is eaten by all the animals, that there may be food for you and for them.
And you shall choose for your sons three maidens, from the daughters of men, and they shall be wives to your sons.
And Noah rose up, and he made the ark, in the place where Elohim had commanded him, and Noah did as Elohim had ordered him.
In his five hundred and ninety-fifth year Noah commenced to make the ark, and he made the ark in five years, as YAHUAH had commanded.
Then Noah took the three daughters of Eliakim, son of Methuselah, for wives for his sons, as YAHUAH had commanded Noah.

And it was at that time Methuselah the son of Enoch died, nine hundred and sixty years old was he, at his death. « • • • Here is one of the most important corrections of modern Christian reading that Jasher supplies. The hundred and twenty years of Genesis 6:3 are often taken as “the new maximum lifespan of human beings,” and entire sermons have been built on that reading. Jasher makes clear it is nothing of the sort. The 120 years are the grace period given before the flood. They are a stay of execution. They are the period during which Noah and Methuselah preached and the earth refused to hear. Peter preserves this reading when he calls Noah “a preacher of righteousness” (2 Peter 2:5) and when he speaks of the longsuffering of God waiting in the days of Noah (1 Peter 3:20). Jasher makes explicit what Peter implies: the 120 years were a sermon series, not a biological fact. This matters because the pattern is still the pattern. YAHUAH is giving the earth another sermon series right now. The awakening remnant is the Noah and Methuselah of the present age. They are preaching day after day, and most of the earth is refusing to listen. The hundred and twenty years is not just an ancient timer. It is the template of every grace period that will ever be given, up to and including the last one. Everyone reading this commentary is living somewhere inside a grace period. The question is not whether the flood is coming — in the last days it is fire rather than water (2 Peter 3:7) — but whether this generation will hear the preacher of righteousness while the door is still open. Verse 10 is as important as verse 8. “The sons of men would not hearken to them, nor incline their ears to their words, and they were stiffnecked.” The rebellion of the pre-flood generation was not ignorance. They had the preaching. They had the warning. They had the visible construction of the ark — a 450-foot-long sermon that stood in their faces for decades. They were not lost because they didn’t know. They were lost because they would not. Hearing alone is not enough. The 1234 filter is ruthless on this point. “He that saith, I know him, and keepeth not his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” The pre-flood generation heard, and did not keep, and died. The same is true in every generation. What you will not do will drown you, no matter what you know. Noah’s delay in marrying (verse 12) until YAHUAH told him to is a small but beautiful detail. He had thought to himself, why beget children if the world is ending? And YAHUAH in verse 14 tells him otherwise. The righteous continue to build and bear and plant even under the shadow of judgment, because YAHUAH’s plan is never only destruction — it is always destruction that serves restoration. Noah was told to raise up children because the seed of promise was going to need a restored earth to multiply on. In an age when many are tempted by despair — why marry, why have children, why invest, everything is coming down — Jasher’s counsel through Noah is still counsel. Build the ark. Marry the wife. Raise the children. Plant the orchard. YAHUAH is not calling the remnant to a cave. He is calling the remnant to carry the seed through. Cross-references: Genesis 6:3; Genesis 6:9–22; 2 Peter 2:5; 1 Peter 3:20; 2 Peter 3:3–10; Hebrews 11:7; Matthew 24:37–39; Isaiah 54:9–10; Jeremiah 29:4–7 (build houses in Babylon).

chapters.title: The Flood Comes

verses.text: At that time, after the death of Methuselah, YAHUAH (the Lord) said to Noah, Go you with your household into the ark; behold I will gather to you all the animals of the earth, the beasts of the field and the fowls of the air, and they shall all come and surround the ark.

And you shall go and seat thyself by the doors of the ark, and all the beasts, the animals, and the fowls, shall assemble and place themselves before you, and such of them as shall come and crouch before you, shall you take and deliver into the hands of your sons, who shall bring them to the ark, and all that will stand before you you shall leave.
And YAHUAH brought this about on the next day, and animals, beasts and fowls came in great multitudes and surrounded the ark.
And Noah went and seated himself by the door of the ark, and of all flesh that crouched before him, he brought into the ark, and all that stood before him he left upon earth.

And a lioness came, with her two whelps, male and female, and the three crouched before Noah, and the two whelps rose up against the lioness and smote her, and made her flee from her place, and she went away, and they returned to their places, and crouched upon the earth before Noah.
And the lioness ran away, and stood in the place of the lions.
And Noah saw this, and wondered greatly, and he rose and took the two whelps, and brought them into the ark.
And Noah brought into the ark from all living creatures that were upon earth, so that there was none left but which Noah brought into the ark.
Two and two came to Noah into the ark, but from the clean animals, and clean fowls, he brought seven couples, as Elohim (God) had commanded him.
And all the animals, and beasts, and fowls, were still there, and they surrounded the ark at every place, and the rain had not descended till seven days after.

And on that day, YAHUAH caused the whole earth to shake, and the sun darkened, and the foundations of the world raged, and the whole earth was moved violently, and the lightning flashed, and the thunder roared, and all the fountains in the earth were broken up, such as was not known to the inhabitants before; and Elohim did this mighty act, in order to terrify the sons of men, that there might be no more evil upon earth.
And still the sons of men would not return from their evil ways, and they increased the anger of YAHUAH at that time, and did not even direct their hearts to all this.
And at the end of seven days, in the six hundredth year of the life of Noah, the waters of the flood were upon the earth.
And all the fountains of the deep were broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened, and the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
And Noah and his household, and all the living creatures that were with him, came into the ark on account of the waters of the flood, and YAHUAH shut him in.

And all the sons of men that were left upon the earth, became exhausted through evil on account of the rain, for the waters were coming more violently upon the earth, and the animals and beasts were still surrounding the ark.
And the sons of men assembled together, about seven hundred thousand men and women, and they came to Noah to the ark.
And they called to Noah, saying, Open for us that we may come to you in the ark–and therefore shall we die?

And Noah, with a loud voice, answered them from the ark, saying, Have you not all rebelled against YAHUAH, and said that he does not exist? and therefore YAHUAH brought upon you this evil, to destroy and cut you off from the face of the earth.
Is not this the thing that I spoke to you of one hundred and twenty years back, and you would not hearken to the voice of YAHUAH, and now do you desire to live upon earth?
And they said to Noah, We are ready to return to YAHUAH; only open for us that we may live and not die.

And Noah answered them, saying, Behold now that you see the trouble of your souls, you wish to return to YAHUAH; why did you not return during these hundred and twenty years, which YAHUAH granted you as the determined period?

But now you come and tell me this on account of the troubles of your souls, now also the YAHUAH will not listen to you, neither will he give ear to you on this day, so that you will not now succeed in your wishes.
And the sons of men approached in order to break into the ark, to come in on account of the rain, for they could not bear the rain upon them.

And YAHUAH sent all the beasts and animals that stood round the ark. And the beasts overpowered them and drove them from that place, and every man went his way and they again scattered themselves upon the face of the earth.

And the rain was still descending upon the earth, and it descended forty days and forty nights, and the waters prevailed greatly upon the earth; and all flesh that was upon the earth or in the waters died, whether men, animals, beasts, creeping things or birds of the air, and there only remained Noah and those that were with him in the ark.
And the waters prevailed and they greatly increased upon the earth, and they lifted up the ark and it was raised from the earth.
And the ark floated upon the face of the waters, and it was tossed upon the waters so that all the living creatures within were turned about like pottage in a cauldron.
And great anxiety seized all the living creatures that were in the ark, and the ark was like to be broken.

And all the living creatures that were in the ark were terrified, and the lions roared, and the oxen lowed, and the wolves howled, and every living creature in the ark spoke and lamented in its own language, so that their voices reached to a great distance, and Noah and his sons cried and wept in their troubles; they were greatly afraid that they had reached the gates of death.

And Noah prayed to YAHUAH, and cried to him on account of this, and he said, O YAHUAH help us, for we have no strength to bear this evil that has encompassed us, for the waves of the waters have surrounded us, mischievous torrents have terrified us, the snares of death have come before us; answer us, O YAHUAH (O Lord), answer us, light up your countenance toward us and be gracious to us, redeem us and deliver us.
And YAHUAH hearkened to the voice of Noah, and YAHUAH remembered him.
And a wind passed over the earth, and the waters were still and the ark rested.
And the fountains of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped, and the rain from heaven was restrained.
And the waters decreased in those days, and the ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat.

And Noah then opened the windows of the ark, and Noah still called out to YAHUAH at that time and he said, O YAHUAH, who did form the earth and the heavens and all that are in it, bring forth our souls from this confinement, and from the prison wherein you have placed us, for I am much wearied with sighing.
And YAHUAH hearkened to the voice of Noah, and said to him, When though shall have completed a full year you shall then go forth.
And at the revolution of the year, when a full year was completed to Noah’s dwelling in the ark, the waters were dried from off the earth, and Noah put off the covering of the ark.
At that time, on the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was dry, but Noah and his sons, and those that were with him, did not go out from the ark until YAHUAH told them.
And the day came that YAHUAH told them to go out, and they all went out from the ark.

And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served YAHUAH all their days, and YAHUAH blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.

And he said to them, Be fruitful and fill all the earth; become strong and increase abundantly in the earth and multiply in it. « • • • Jasher 6:17–22 is one of the most sobering passages in all of apocryphal literature. Seven hundred thousand men and women came to the ark after the rain began, begging to be let in. And they were not. This is the side of the flood story that gets cropped out of children’s Bibles — the side where the people you thought were going to just die blithely in their sleep are actually pounding on the side of the ark while Noah answers them from the other side of a sealed door. Jasher verse 15 is even more striking: “and YAHUAH shut him in.” The door of the ark was not shut by Noah. It was shut by YAHUAH Himself. This is the pattern YAHUSHA warned of in Matthew 25 with the parable of the ten virgins. The door gets shut, and the late arrivals knock, and the answer from inside is “I do not know you.” The late repentance offered in the middle of the flood is not received as repentance — it is received as the self-interested cry of the drowning. That is not a contradiction of the gospel of grace. It is the gospel of grace properly understood. Grace is offered during the grace period. When the grace period closes, what looks like repentance is only panic. The 1234 of truth applies here too: genuine repentance shows itself by keeping His commandments, and if that fruit has not grown during the window of grace, the fruitless cry at the end is not the fruit He was looking for. It does not mean the modern reader should be hard. It means the modern reader should be sober. We are still inside a grace period. The door has not shut yet. Whoever you love who is outside the ark, you speak to them while you still can. Don’t let the rain start and find that you waited because you thought there would always be more time. Verse 30 — every living creature in the ark spoke and lamented in its own language — is one of the most tender verses in scripture, and it is not in Genesis. The animals in the ark groaned under the judgment of creation as the ship pitched. The apostle Paul would later write that “the whole creation groans and travails together in pain until now” (Romans 8:22), waiting for the manifestation of the sons of Elohim. Jasher gives us a glimpse of the first groaning. The animals felt the judgment. The righteous in the ark cried through it with them. The scattered seed in exile has always groaned through the judgment of the systems around them. The groaning is heard. YAHUAH remembered Noah (Jasher 6:32; Genesis 8:1), and the wind passed, and the ark rested. The ark resting on the mountains of Ararat (verse 35) is the first “resting” of anything after the flood, and the name Ararat in Hebrew is connected to the root meaning curse reversed. The earth had been cursed since Adam; the curse had deepened under the flood; and on that mountain the ark came to rest, and the seed of a new earth stepped out. Every time YAHUAH comes to rescue a scattered, groaning people, there is always a mountain where the vessel comes to rest. For the remnant in the last days, the mountain is Zion (Micah 4:1–2). The ark of the seed will rest again, and the door will open again, and the land will be told once more “be fruitful and fill all the earth” (Jasher 6:42; Genesis 9:1). Flood theology and the eight as covenant remnant architecture The flood is the first great seed-war winnowing, and the eight preserved are not a symbol. They are a structure. Every numbered remnant in scripture afterward — the two hundred and seventy of Gideon's screened warriors, the seven thousand who had not bowed the knee to Baal in Elijah's day, the hundred and forty-four thousand of Revelation 7, the exact count Yahuah (God) knows of the tribes He is gathering — follows the architectural template of the eight-preserved. A specific, countable, named remnant out of a multitude. Not a crowd. Not a spiritual category. A number the Shepherd can call by name. Why eight. Seven is the number of the completion of the first creation — six days of work, one day of rest, the full cycle of what was made. Eight is the number of the first day of the new creation. The flood ended the first world. The family that stepped out of the ark onto the mountain of Ararat were the first inhabitants of the second earth. Eight souls. Eight witnesses. Eight names Yahuah (God) knew. "By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of Elohim (God) waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water" (1 Peter 3:19–20). The apostle Peter counted them. He did not round. He did not say several or a few families. He said eight. The exact number was load-bearing enough for the apostle to name it specifically. This is why circumcision was given on the eighth day. Yahuah (God) did not pick the day at random. Every covenant son marked in the flesh on the eighth day is being marked as a son of the new-creation remnant. The first eight came through water. Every Hebrew son after them would be marked on the day that matched their number. The architecture of the eight is written into the body of every covenant male for four thousand years. Even now, in the houses that observe the command, every brit milah at eight days is a rehearsal of the flood-remnant pattern. The son whose blood is shed on the eighth day is being marked as one more addition to the count of those Yahuah (God) knows by name. The flood itself was not the Father losing patience with humanity in a general sense. It was the Father's response to a specific emergency. Genesis 6:9 says Noah was tamim in his generations — a word usually translated perfect but which in its primary sense means unblemished, whole, without admixture. Animal offerings are tamim because they have no defect. Noah's being tamim in his generations is not a moral claim; it is a claim about his line. His seed had not been mixed. The Watcher-gene had not penetrated his lineage. He was a son of Adam whose Adamic integrity was still intact. This is why Yahuah (God) chose him. The flood was a precision instrument. It was designed to remove the corruption the Watchers had spread through almost all flesh, and to preserve the one line that had not been touched. "And Elohim (God) saw the earth, and, behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted his way upon the earth" (Genesis 6:12). The word flesh there is the Hebrew basar, which can include animals as well as humans. The Book of Enoch tells us the giants had begun to sin against birds and beasts and reptiles and fish (1 Enoch 7:5), and Jasher tells us that the sons of men had taught the mixture of animals of one species with the other to provoke Yahuah (Jasher 4:18). The corruption was not only in the human line; it had spread into the animal kingdom. The flood cleansed both. The ark carried only clean animals in sevens and unclean animals in pairs (Genesis 7:2) — a commandment that distinguished clean from unclean before Sinai, given to Noah as naturally as the command to be fruitful had been given to Adam. Torah was in the ark before it was on the tablets. The distinctions of Leviticus were already being enforced at Ararat. The door shut by Yahuah (God) Himself in Jasher 6:15 is the most sobering line in the chapter, and the parable of the ten virgins picks it up verbatim. "And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut. Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Adon (Lord), Adon (Lord), open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not" (Matthew 25:10–12). The seven hundred thousand pounding on the outside of the ark are the five foolish virgins of Matthew 25. Same door. Same voice from the inside. Same late knocking that arrives too late. The grammar of the grace period closing is identical across both texts because it is the same grammar. Yahuah (God) opens the door for a determined season. Those who have prepared enter. Those who delayed knock after. The knock is heard — but the door is not reopened. This is not cruelty. It is the specific mercy of a specific season that gave notice and kept it. The door was open for a hundred and twenty years. It was shut for one rain. That is the pattern. The 144,000 of Revelation 7 are the flood-remnant architecture in final form. Twelve thousand sealed of each of the twelve tribes — Yahudah (Judah) twelve thousand, Reuben twelve thousand, Gad twelve thousand, Asher twelve thousand, Naphtali twelve thousand, Manasseh twelve thousand, Simeon twelve thousand, Levi twelve thousand, Issachar twelve thousand, Zebulun twelve thousand, Joseph twelve thousand, Benjamin twelve thousand. "And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)" (Revelation 7:4). Note what the text says and does not say. It does not say a symbolic number representing all believers. It does not say a spiritual group of whoever chose to identify with Yashar'el (Israel). It says of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and then it names the tribes. The scattered seed of Yahuah's (God's) covenant people is being gathered by name in specific numbers. That gathering mirrors the gathering Noah's family underwent at the door of the ark. A countable number. A Shepherd who knows each name. A specific preservation of a specific people out of a specific judgment. The eight became the 144,000. The Father has been tracking the count since Noah, and He has been tracking the count through every dispersion since. Say the 144,000 is a spiritual category open to any believer and you have broken the architecture. You have collapsed the distinction Yahuah (God) has been maintaining since Genesis 6. The text will not let you do that. The tribes are named. The number is counted. The scattered seed is coming home, and the Shepherd is calling them by name the way He called out the eight when He shut the door. The seven hundred thousand who came to the ark after the rain began are not props in a warning story. They are the pattern. Read Jasher 6:17–22 with the compassion the voice of this commentary requires. Most of those who pounded on the door of the ark were children of the same Adam Noah descended from. They had heard a hundred and twenty years of preaching. They had watched a boat being built for a rain that had never come. They had laughed. They had mocked. They had gone about their business. They had drunk their barrenness-draughts and glazed their idols and shaded their eyelids with the antimony Azâzêl had taught. And when the water came up around their feet, they ran for the boat. And the boat would not open. And they died with their faces pressed against wood they had despised. The people still inside the systems of this age have inherited the same kind of despising from their fathers. The Catholic priest who was taught by his seminary that the Torah is shadow. The Protestant elder who was taught by his pastor that Sabbath is Sunday. The Torah-observant teacher who was taught by his rabbi that the Messiah (Christ) cannot be Yahusha (Jesus). The imam who was taught by his sheikh that the covenant transferred to Ishmael. Every one of them is a person standing near a boat they have not yet seen. The awakening remnant is not their enemy. The awakening remnant is the Noah who is still preaching. The flood has not yet come. The door has not yet shut. Whoever has ears still has time. The Father is patient in the way Peter said He was patient — "not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance" (2 Peter 3:9). But patience is not the same as endless patience. The door was open for a hundred and twenty years, and then it was shut in a day. Every grace period ends. The question for the reader standing outside the ark is not whether the Father is loving. He is loving. The question is whether the reader will walk through the door while the walking is still possible. Cross-references: Genesis 7:1–24; Genesis 8:1–22; Matthew 24:37–39; Matthew 25:1–13; Luke 13:25; 2 Peter 2:5; 2 Peter 3:5–7; Hebrews 11:7; Romans 8:19–23; Micah 4:1–2; Isaiah 54:9; 1 Peter 3:19–20; Genesis 6:9; Genesis 6:12; Genesis 7:2; Matthew 25:10–12; Revelation 7:4–8; 1 Enoch 7:5; 2 Peter 3:9; Hebrews 11:7; Genesis 17:12 (eighth-day circumcision).

chapters.title: The Table of Nations and the Rise of Nimrod — The First

verses.text: And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.
These are the sons of Japheth; Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, seven sons.
And the sons of Gomer were Askinaz, Rephath and Tegarmah.
And the sons of Magog were Elichanaf and Lubal.
And the children of Madai were Achon, Zeelo, Chazoni and Lot.
And the sons of Javan were Elisha, Tarshish, Chittim and Dudonim.
And the sons of Tubal were Ariphi, Kesed and Taari.
And the sons of Meshech were Dedon, Zaron and Shebashni.
And the sons of Tiras were Benib, Gera, Lupirion and Gilak; these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, and their numbers in those days were about four hundred and sixty men.
And these are the sons of Ham; Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan, four sons; and the sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama and Satecha, and the sons of Raama were Sheba and Dedan.
And the sons of Mitzraim were Lud, Anom and Pathros, Chasloth and Chaphtor.
And the sons of Phut were Gebul, Hadan, Benah and Adan.
And the sons of Canaan were Zidon, Heth, Amori, Gergashi, Hivi, Arkee, Seni, Arodi, Zimodi and Chamothi.
These are the sons of Ham, according to their families, and their numbers in those days were about seven hundred and thirty men.
And these are the sons of Shem; Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram, five sons; and the sons of Elam were Shushan, Machul and Harmon.
And the sons of Ashar were Mirus and Mokil, and the sons of Arpachshad were Shelach, Anar and Ashcol.
And the sons of Lud were Pethor and Bizayon, and the sons of Aram were Uz, Chul, Gather and Mash.

These are the sons of Shem, according to their families; and their numbers in those days were about three hundred men. 15 19. These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided. 20. And the name of the second was Yoktan, meaning that in his day the lives of the sons of men were diminished and lessened. 21. These are the sons of Yoktan; Almodad, Shelaf, Chazarmoveth, Yerach, Hadurom, Ozel, Diklah, Obal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah and Jobab; all these are the sons of Yoktan. 22. And Peleg his brother begat Yen, and Yen begat Serug, and Serug begat Nahor and Nahor begat Terah, and Terah was thirty-eight years old, and he begat Haran and Nahor. 23. And Cush the son of Ham, the son of Noah, took a wife in those days in his old age, and she bare a son, and they called his name Nimrod, saying, At that time the sons of men again began to rebel and transgress against Elohim (God), and the child grew up, and his father loved him exceedingly, for he was the son of his old age. 24. And the garments of skin which Elohim made for Adam and his wife, when they went out of the garden, were given to Cush. 25. For after the death of Adam and his wife, the garments were given to Enoch, the son of Jared, and when Enoch was taken up to Elohim, he gave them to Methuselah, his son. 26. And at the death of Methuselah, Noah took them and brought them to the ark, and they were with him until he went out of the ark. 27. And in their going out, Ham stole those garments from Noah his father, and he took them and hid them from his brothers. 28. And when Ham begat his first born Cush, he gave him the garments in secret, and they were with Cush many days. 29. And Cush also concealed them from his sons and brothers, and when Cush had begotten Nimrod, he gave him those garments through his love for him, and Nimrod grew up, and when he was twenty years old he put on those garments. 30. And Nimrod became strong when he put on the garments, and Elohim gave him might and strength, and he was a mighty hunter in the earth, yea, he was a mighty hunter in the field, and he hunted the animals and he built altars, and he offered upon them the animals before YAHUAH (the Lord). 31. And Nimrod strengthened himself, and he rose up from amongst his brethren, and he fought the battles of his brethren against all their enemies round about. 32. And YAHUAH delivered all the enemies of his brethren in his hands, and Elohim prospered him from time to time in his battles, and he reigned upon earth. 33. Therefore it became current in those days, when a man ushered forth those that he had trained up for battle, he would say to them, Like Elohim did to Nimrod, who was a mighty hunter in the earth, and who succeeded in the battles that prevailed against his brethren, that he delivered them from the hands of their enemies, so may Elohim strengthen us and deliver us this day. 34. And when Nimrod was forty years old, at that time there was a war between his brethren and the children of Japheth, so that they were in the power of their enemies. 35. And Nimrod went forth at that time, and he assembled all the sons of Cush and their families, about four hundred and sixty men, and he hired also from some of his friends and acquaintances about eighty men, and be gave them their hire, and he went with them to battle, and when he was on the road, Nimrod strengthened the hearts of the people that went with him. 36. And he said to them, Do not fear, neither be alarmed, for all our enemies will be delivered into our hands, and you may do with them as you please. 37. And all the men that went were about five hundred, and they fought against their enemies, and they destroyed them, and subdued them, and Nimrod placed standing officers over them in their respective places. 38. And he took some of their children as security, and they were all servants to Nimrod and to his brethren, and Nimrod and all the people that were with him turned homeward. 39. And when Nimrod had joyfully returned from battle, after having conquered his enemies, all his brethren, together with those who knew him before, assembled to make him king over them, and they placed the regal crown upon his head. 40. And he set over his subjects and people, princes, judges, and rulers, as is the custom amongst kings. 41. And he placed Terah the son of Nahor the prince of his host, and he dignified him and elevated him above all his princes. 42. And whilst he was reigning according to his heart’s desire, after having conquered all his enemies around, he advised with his counselors to build a city for his palace, and they did so. 43. And they found a large valley opposite to the east, and they built him a large and extensive city, and Nimrod called the name of the city that he built Shinar, for YAHUAH had vehemently shaken his enemies and destroyed them. 44. And Nimrod dwelt in Shinar, and he reigned securely, and he fought with his enemies and he subdued them, and he prospered in all his battles, and his kingdom became very great. 45. And all nations and tongues heard of his fame, and they gathered themselves to him, and they bowed down to the earth, and they brought him offerings, and he became their Lord and king, and they all dwelt with him in the city at Shinar, and Nimrod reigned in the earth over all the sons of Noah, and they were all under his power and counsel. 46. And all the earth was of one tongue and words of union, but Nimrod did not go in the ways of YAHUAH, and he was more wicked than all the men that were before him, from the days of the flood until those days. 47. And he made gods of wood and stone, and he bowed down to them, and he rebelled against YAHUAH, and taught all his subjects and the people of the earth his wicked ways; and Mardon his son was more wicked than his father. 48. And every one that heard of the acts of Mardon the son of Nimrod would say, concerning him, From the wicked goes forth wickedness; therefore it became a proverb in the whole earth, saying, From the wicked goes forth wickedness, and it was current in the words of men from that time to this. 49. And Terah the son of Nahor, prince of Nimrod’s host, was in those days very great in the sight of the king and his subjects, and the king and princes loved him, and they elevated him very high. 50. And Terah took a wife and her name was Amthelo the daughter of Cornebo; and the wife of Terah conceived and bare him a son in those days. 51. Terah was seventy years old when he begat him, and Terah called the name of his son that was born to him Abram, because the king had raised him in those days, and dignified him above all his princes that were with him. « • • • Jasher chapter 7 is one of the most important chapters in the entire book for understanding the prophetic shape of scripture, because in it we are introduced to the first great adversary of the covenant seed: Nimrod. Every subsequent kingdom of the world that rises up against YAHUAH’s people carries something of Nimrod in it. Babel/Babylon is his city.
