Nineveh, founded by Ashur who fled from Nimrod (verse related; compare Genesis 10:11), carries his shadow. Egypt carries it. Rome carries it. Every system that tries to unify humanity under one tongue, one religion, one currency, one king who is not YAHUSHA carries the Nimrod pattern. When Revelation 17 and 18 describe Babylon the Great, the harlot riding the beast, the pattern is traceable all the way back to Jasher 7. The detail about Adam’s garments is one of Jasher’s most discussed passages. Jasher tells us that the garments of skin which YAHUAH made for Adam and Eve when He expelled them from the garden — the first covering made from a slain animal, the first blood shed for the covering of sin — were passed down through the generations: Adam to Enoch to Methuselah to Noah, onto the ark, and then stolen by Ham and given to Cush and then to Nimrod. When Nimrod put them on, he was clothed in mighty strength. This is a dark and important tradition. The physical garments represented the first covenant covering — the first gospel picture of blood shed to clothe the naked sinner. Ham stole them. Cush hoarded them. Nimrod wore them and used the authority they represented against YAHUAH. This is a prefiguration of every false religious system that clothes itself in the symbols of the true covenant while operating in rebellion against the true covenant’s author. The Catholic system has inherited the language of the gospel while the operation is Nimrodic. Islam has inherited the Abrahamic line while the operation is idolatrous. Even — and this is the hard part for Hebrew roots readers — even Torah-observant communities can wear Torah garments while operating in a Nimrod spirit, if the Torah becomes a means of building a tower to the heavens by one’s own strength rather than a gift for walking humbly with YAHUAH. Every garment stolen from the covenant and worn in rebellion is a Nimrodic garment. Verse 30 is delicate. “And Elohim gave him might and strength, and he was a mighty hunter in the earth.” Jasher says YAHUAH Himself gave Nimrod his initial strength. This is not YAHUAH endorsing Nimrod. It is YAHUAH preserving His own sovereignty over all that happens. Every gift can be turned into rebellion by the one who receives it. Nimrod’s strength was a gift. What he did with it was his own choice. Paul will later write that YAHUAH gave even Pharaoh his throne for the purpose of making His name known (Romans 9:17). YAHUAH’s sovereignty over the rise of wicked kings does not make them innocent. It makes them accountable in a deeper way. Verse 46 — “all the earth was of one tongue and words of union” — is a foreshadow of what is about to happen at Babel in chapter 9. Nimrod’s project is to weld mankind into one unit under one human king. This is the oldest anti-YAHUAH dream in scripture, and it is still the dream of the last-days beast (Revelation 13:7–8). Every time you hear a world leader call for global unification under a unified system — one currency, one religion, one consciousness, one AI — you are hearing Nimrod’s dream resurrected. The word for this dream in scripture is Babel, and we will meet it properly in chapter 9. And verse 51 — “Terah called the name of his son that was born to him Abram” — is the hinge. In the middle of Nimrod’s empire, in the capital city of the first global anti-covenant kingdom, a righteous child is born into the house of Nimrod’s own chief of staff. YAHUAH never leaves Himself without a seed. Wherever the darkness thickens, there He plants a light. Table of Nations as the scattered-seed map and Nimrod's archetype Before we follow Nimrod further into his tower-building, two architectural truths about Jasher 7 need naming, because without them the rest of the prophetic canon cannot be read properly. The first is that the seventy nations of the Table are not a genealogical curiosity. They are the prophetic map of where the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) would later be sown. The second is that Nimrod's empire is the archetype whose shadow falls on every anti-covenant kingdom from Babel to the last-days beast of Revelation. Deuteronomy 32:8 in the Septuagint and Dead Sea Scrolls manuscripts reads: "When the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Elohim (God)." The later Masoretic tradition read sons of Yashar'el (Israel) in that verse, but the older reading preserved in the Greek and the Qumran scrolls is sons of Elohim (God) — the seventy heavenly overseers Jasher 9:32 names explicitly: "Elohim (God) said to the seventy angels who stood foremost before him, to those who were near to him, saying, Come let us descend and confuse their tongues." Seventy angels. Seventy nations. The earth was divided, at Babel, into seventy territorial inheritances, each assigned to a heavenly supervisor. Psalm 82 is the arraignment of those supervisors: "Elohim (God) standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the elohim (gods). How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?" (Psalm 82:1–2). The gods of the nations are real. They are lesser beings. They were delegated authorities who rebelled and began to be worshiped as gods. The final gathering of the scattered seed includes, as its last act, the judgment of those fallen delegates. Daniel 10:13 and 10:20 confirm the architecture — the prince of Persia and the prince of Greece are real heavenly princes, not mere political metaphors, and the angel who came to Daniel fought his way through them. This is why the Table of Nations matters so much. Yahuah (God) did not scatter mankind arbitrarily at Babel. He distributed the nations into named territories under named overseers. The Japhethite lines — Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras — went north and west, into the lands Jasher 10 identifies with France, Germany, Italy, Greece, the Mediterranean coasts, and the lands of Togarmah reaching into the Caucasus and eastern Europe. The Hamitic lines went south and east — Egypt, Cush, Phut, and Canaan. The Shemitic lines stayed in the Near East — Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram. And then, when the time came for the covenant people to be scattered by judgment, they were not scattered into empty space. They were scattered into territories already assigned, already inhabited, already under named supervisors. The Assyrian exile in 722 BCE carried the ten northern tribes into Media, into the Caucasus, into the isles of the Gentiles along the trade routes that the sons of Japheth had opened for them centuries before. The Babylonian exile of 586 BCE carried Yahudah (Judah) into Mesopotamia, into the region Nimrod himself had first civilized. The Roman dispersion of 70 CE scattered the remaining people into the lands the Romans had conquered — which is to say, into the lands the sons of Japheth had previously settled. This is exactly the geography the prophets named. "Hear the word of Yahuah (the Lord), O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Yashar'el (Israel) will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock" (Jeremiah 31:10). The isles afar off are the Japhethite distributions of Jasher 10. Isaiah's call in chapter 49 is to the same territory: "Listen, O isles, unto me; and hearken, ye people, from far; Yahuah (the Lord) hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name" (Isaiah 49:1). The Servant Song is addressed to the isles — the scattered seed among the Japhethite nations is being called to listen. Isaiah 11:11 counts the places from which the second gathering will come: "And it shall come to pass in that day, that Yahuah (the Lord) shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left, from Assyria, and from Egypt, and from Pathros, and from Cush, and from Elam, and from Shinar, and from Hamath, and from the islands of the sea." Every one of those regions is named in Jasher 7–10. The gathering is not happening from Christian denominational affiliations. It is happening from specific territories settled by specific sons of Noah, into which scattered Yashar'el (Israel) was later seeded. This is the dismantling of the Hebrew Roots inclusion gospel that every teacher in that movement must eventually reckon with. The claim that any sincere Torah-keeper is thereby counted as Yashar'el (Israel) — that faith-plus-obedience confers covenant identity without regard to bloodline — collapses the prophetic geography into meaninglessness. If Yashar'el (Israel) is a spiritual category open to whoever shows up with the right practices, then Isaiah 11 does not know where to look, and Jeremiah 31 has no flock to recover, and Isaiah 49:1's isles are a rhetorical flourish rather than a specific address. The prophets were not speaking abstractly. They were speaking to a specific people in specific places. The scattered seed was a real people who went into real lands, and the gathering is a real operation Yahuah (God) is carrying out now — not by any believer's act of self-identification but by the Father's own sovereign calling. The one who hears the call and comes home is not making himself Yashar'el (Israel) by deciding to; he is being revealed as Yashar'el (Israel) because the Shepherd is calling by name. The nations for their part are not discarded. The Father loves them. The prophets promise that the righteous among the nations will accompany the scattered seed home: "And the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place: and the house of Yashar'el (Israel) shall possess them in the land of Yahuah (the Lord)" (Isaiah 14:1–2). And Zechariah's word still stands: "Thus saith Yahuah (the Lord) of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Yahudi (Jew), saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that Elohim (God) is with you" (Zechariah 8:23). The nations come home with the seed. The distinction between the seed and the stranger is maintained — both loved, both welcomed, both coming home — and the stranger who walks with the covenant household is not absorbed into the seed. He is a stranger-and-sojourner honored in the covenant household forever. This is the provision Torah made at Sinai for the mixed multitude who came up out of Egypt, and it is the provision that holds at the end of the age. Loved without being seed. Seated at the table without being reassigned the bloodline. The distinction is real and permanent, and the distinction is merciful. And now, with that architecture in mind, we can turn to Nimrod — because Nimrod is the first man to try to break it. Nimrod's project was not merely to build a city and a tower. His project was to unify the nations Yahuah (God) had just distributed, under a single human crown, in a way that would make the seventy inheritances unnecessary. That ambition is the archetype. Every empire that has tried to weld the nations back into one under a single anti-covenant authority — Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, Rome, and every reiteration of the Babylonian spirit since — is working from Nimrod's blueprint. The spirit of Nimrod is the spirit of anti-distribution. The Father distributed. Nimrod wants to re-aggregate. The Father named seventy overseers. Nimrod wants one throne. The Father confused the tongues. Nimrod and his heirs keep rebuilding the one tongue — whether in Latin or in Greek or in English or in the common tongue of global finance and global media and global technology that now threatens to close over the earth again. The sovereignty language in Jasher 7:30 — "Elohim (God) gave him might and strength, and he was a mighty hunter in the earth" — is the same language Paul would later use of Pharaoh: "For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth" (Romans 9:17). Every wicked king who has ever risen has risen by permission. The permission does not excuse the wickedness. The permission means that even the rebellion is woven into the story Yahuah (God) is telling, to make His power known to the ends of the earth. Nimrod's rise serves the testimony of Nimrod's fall. The beast's rise serves the testimony of the beast's fall. The Father is not responding to history. He is writing it — and the villains in it do not have a page He did not account for in advance. Cross-references: Genesis 10:1–32; Genesis 11:1–9; Genesis 3:21 (garments of skin); Micah 5:6 (the land of Nimrod); Isaiah 14:13–14; Revelation 13:1–18; Revelation 17:1–18:24; Romans 9:17; Jude 1:11; 2 Thessalonians 2:3–4; Deuteronomy 32:8–9 (LXX/DSS reading); Psalm 82:1–8; Daniel 10:13, 20; Jeremiah 31:10; Isaiah 49:1; Isaiah 11:11–12; Isaiah 14:1–2; Zechariah 8:23; Romans 9:17; Jeremiah 16:14–15; Ezekiel 39:27–28.

chapters.title: The Star at Abram’s Birth, and the King Who Tried to Kill the

verses.text: And it was in the night that Abram was born, that all the servants of Terah, and all the wise men of Nimrod, and his conjurors came and ate and drank in the house of Terah, and they rejoiced with him on that night.

And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.
And all the wise men of the king and his conjurors were astonished at the sight, and the sages understood this matter, and they knew its import.

And they said to each other, This only betokens the child that has been born to Terah this night, who will grow up and be fruitful, and multiply, and possess all the earth, he and his children for ever, and he and his seed will slay great kings, and inherit their lands.
And the wise men and conjurors went home that night, and in the morning all these wise men and conjurors rose up early, and assembled in an appointed house.
And they spoke and said to each other, Behold the sight that we saw last night is hidden from the king, it has not been made known to him.

And should this thing get known to the king in the latter days, he will say to us, Why have you concealed this matter from me, and then we shall all suffer death; therefore, now let us go and tell the king the sight which we saw, and the interpretation of it, and we shall then remain clear.
And they did so, and they all went to the king and bowed down to him to the ground, and they said, May the king live, may the king live.
We heard that a son was born to Terah the son of Nahor, the prince of your host, and we yesternight came to his house, and we ate and drank and rejoiced with him that night.

And when your servants went out from the house of Terah, to go to our respective homes to abide there for the night, we lifted up our eyes to heaven, and we saw a great star coming from the east, and the same star ran with great speed, and swallowed up four great stars, from the four sides of the heavens.

And your servants were astonished at the sight which we saw, and were greatly terrified, and we made our judgment upon the sight, and knew by our wisdom the proper interpretation of it, that this thing applies to the child that is born to Terah, who will grow up and multiply greatly, and become powerful, and kill all the kings of the earth, and inherit all their lands, he and his seed forever.
And now our Lord and king, behold we have truly acquainted you with what we have seen concerning this child.

If it seems good to the king to give his father value for this child, we will slay him before he shall grow up and increase in the land, and his evil increase against us, that we and our children perish through his evil.
And the king heard their words and they seemed good in his sight, and he sent and called for Terah, and Terah came before the king.
And the king said to Terah, I have been told that a son was yesternight born to you, and after this manner was observed in the heavens at his birth.
And now therefore give me the child, that we may slay him before his evil springs up against us, and I will give you for his value, your house full of silver and gold.
And Terah answered the king and said to him: My Lord and king, I have heard your words, and your servant shall do all that his king desires.

But my Lord and king, I will tell you what happened to me yesternight, that I may see what advice the king will give his servant, and then I will answer the king upon what he has just spoken; and the king said, Speak.
And Terah said to the king, Ayon, son of Mored, came to me yesternight, saying,

Give to me the great and beautiful horse that the king gave you, and I will give you silver and gold, and straw and provender for its value; and I said to him, Wait till I see the king concerning your words, and behold whatever the king says, that will I do.
And now my Lord and king, behold I have made this thing known to you, and the advice which my king will give to his servant, that will I follow.
And the king heard the words of Terah, and his anger was kindled and he considered him in the light of a fool.

And the king answered Terah, and he said to him, Are you so silly, ignorant, or deficient in understanding, to do this thing, to give your beautiful horse for silver and gold or even for straw and provender?

Are you so short of silver and gold, that you should do this thing, because you can not obtain straw and provender to feed your horse? and what is silver and gold to you, or straw and provender, that you should give away that fine horse which I gave you, like which there is none to be had on the whole earth?
And the king left off speaking, and Terah answered the king, saying, Like to this has the king spoken to his servant;

I beseech you, my Lord and king, what is this which you did say to me, saying, Give your son that we may slay him, and I will give you silver and gold for his value; what shall I do with silver and gold after the death of my son? who shall inherit me? surely then at my death, the silver and gold will return to my king who gave it.
And when the king heard the words of Terah, and the parable which he brought concerning the king, it grieved him greatly and he was vexed at this thing, and his anger burned within him.

And Terah saw that the anger of the king was kindled against him, and he answered the king, saying, All that I have is in the king’s power; whatever the king desires to do to his servant, that let him do, yea, even my son, he is in the king’s power, without value in exchange, he and his two brothers that are older than he.
And the king said to Terah, No, but I will purchase your younger son for a price.

And Terah answered the king, saying, I beseech you my Lord and king to let your servant speak a word before you, and let the king hear the word of his servant, and Terah said, Let my king give me three days’ time till I consider this matter within myself, and consult with my family concerning the words of my king; and he pressed the king greatly to agree to this.

And the king hearkened to Terah, and he did so and he gave him three days’ time, and Terah went out from the king’s presence, and he came home to his family and spoke to them all the words of the king; and the people were greatly afraid.

And it was in the third day that the king sent to Terah, saying, Send me your son for a price as I spoke to you; and should you not do this, I will send and slay all you have in your house, so that you shall not even have a dog remaining.

And Terah hastened, (as the thing was urgent from the king), and he took a child from one of his servants, which his handmaid had born to him that day, and Terah brought the child to the king and received value for him.

And YAHUAH (the Lord) was with Terah in this matter, that Nimrod might not cause Abram’s death, and the king took the child from Terah and with all his might dashed his head to the ground, for he thought it had been Abram; and this was concealed from him from that day, and it was forgotten by the king, as it was the will of Providence not to suffer Abram’s death.
And Terah took Abram his son secretly, together with his mother and nurse, and he concealed them in a cave, and he brought them their provisions monthly.

And YAHUAH was with Abram in the cave and he grew up, and Abram was in the cave ten years, and the king and his princes, soothsayers and sages, thought that the king had killed Abram. « • • • Chapter 8 of Jasher is astonishing, and it is the reason so many readers of the apocrypha feel, when they read it for the first time, like they have stumbled into a prequel they did not know existed. The star that appeared at Abram’s birth. The wise men (soothsayers) of a pagan king interpreting it. The king who tried to kill the covenant child. The father who hid the child. The cave of hiding for ten years while the child grew up under the protection of YAHUAH. The pattern is unmistakable. This is the pattern that will recur thirty-nine generations later at the birth of the Messiah. A star appears. Wise men see it. A king is told about it. The king tries to kill the child. A parent (Joseph, in the Messiah’s case; Terah, in Abram’s) hides the child. The covenant seed is preserved through the attempted slaughter, and grows up under YAHUAH’s direct protection. This is not coincidence. This is prophetic typology written into history. Jasher confirms that the Messiah-pattern was already present at Abraham. The covenant head was attacked in infancy. The covenant Messiah was attacked in infancy. The covenant remnant in the last days, Revelation 12 tells us, is also attacked the moment it is born and flees to a prepared wilderness for a season. The birth of every carrier of the seed is attended by a murderous king and a hidden cave. This is the pattern of the age we live in, and of every age. Notice Jasher verse 33: Terah took a child from one of his servants, which his handmaid had born to him that day, and brought that child to Nimrod in place of Abram. The king dashed that child’s head to the ground, thinking it was Abram. An innocent child died in Abram’s place so that Abram might live. This too is a prefiguration. Every covenant child the enemy has tried to kill has had an innocent substitute somewhere in the story — the children of Bethlehem who died in place of the infant Messiah (Matthew 2:16–18), the children of the Hebrews drowned in the Nile while Moses was hidden in a basket (Exodus 1:22). In the final unveiling, the Lamb Himself becomes the innocent substitute who dies for all the other children. The Messiah did not have to have a substitute; He was the substitute. The whole typology points forward to the one who would fulfill it. Jasher verse 34 says “YAHUAH was with Terah in this matter, that Nimrod might not cause Abram’s death… it was the will of Providence not to suffer Abram’s death.” YAHUAH’s hand is sovereign over every royal decree. Every king who has ever tried to wipe out the seed of promise has been thwarted by an unseen providence. Pharaoh — thwarted by midwives and a basket. Haman — thwarted by an insomniac king and a sleepless queen. Herod — thwarted by a dream and a donkey. And in the last days, the final king who tries to wipe out the seed — the one Revelation 13 calls the beast — will be thwarted by the return of the King of kings Himself (Revelation 19:11–21). The cave of Abram’s hiding is the pattern of every cave in which YAHUAH has ever preserved His witnesses (1 Kings 19:9 — Elijah in the cave; Hebrews 11:38 — they wandered in caves and in dens of the earth). And notice — Abram spent ten years in a cave while Nimrod forgot about him. Ten years of silence. Ten years of being sheltered and taught by his mother and nurse while the world went on thinking he was dead. The awakening remnant often endures long silent years of this kind. Years in which the covenant child seems to have been lost, in which the world has written us off, in which no one is paying attention. Those years are never wasted. YAHUAH was with Abram in the cave (verse 36). Whatever cave He has put you in, He is there too. The coming out happens in His timing, not Nimrod’s. The infant-under-a-death-decree pattern, recapitulated across every Nimrodic regime The star, the king's counselors, the decree on the infant, the father hiding the child — this pattern is not a single flourish of Jasher 8. It is the recurring signature of every Nimrodic regime in scripture. Trace it forward. Pharaoh decrees the drowning of the Hebrew male infants in Exodus 1:22, and the one through whom the Exodus will come is hidden in an ark of bulrushes on the same river the decree was meant to use for the drowning. Athaliah seizes the throne of Yahudah (Judah) and slaughters the royal seed of the house of David, and a single infant — Joash — is hidden in the house of Yahuah (the Lord) for six years by a priestly aunt (2 Kings 11:1–3, 2 Chronicles 22:10–12). Herod, hearing of the star the wise men followed, decrees the slaughter of the male infants of Bethlehem under two years old, and the one the star is for is taken by night into Egypt by a father warned in a dream (Matthew 2:13–18). And in the last days, Revelation 12 tells us the woman clothed with the sun — the covenant community from which the Messiah (Christ) came and through which the scattered seed is being regathered — is pursued into the wilderness and nourished there for a season the book counts in days: "And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of Elohim (God), that they should feed her there a thousand two hundred and threescore days" (Revelation 12:6). The infant-under-a-decree is always hidden. The hidden one is always preserved. The decree always fails. Every time the enemy has tried to wipe out the covenant seed at its birth, an unseen providence has moved the pieces. A midwife in Egypt who feared Elohim (God) more than she feared Pharaoh. A princess drawing a basket out of the Nile. An aunt in the temple. A husband in a dream. A flight into the same Egypt from which the covenant once fled. The Father has never been without an Eliezer in the enemy's court, a Jochebed in the enemy's city, a Bathia in the enemy's house. The ark of Noah preserved the seed through the flood. The ark of Moses preserved the seed through the decree. The cave of Abram preserved the seed through the king. The wilderness of the woman in Revelation 12 will preserve the seed through the beast. Every era has its ark. Every remnant is hidden somewhere the enemy cannot see. The specific detail Jasher 8:33 gives — that Terah offered one of his servants' infants in Abram's place, and that Nimrod dashed that infant's head to the ground thinking it was Abram — is a prefiguration that should make the reader pause. An innocent child died in Abram's place that Abram might live. The children of Bethlehem died in the Messiah's (Christ's) place that the Messiah (Christ) might grow. The Hebrew infants drowned in the Nile that Moses might be drawn out. The servants' child in Jasher, the infants of Bethlehem in Matthew, the infants of Egypt in Exodus — all are innocent substitutes whose deaths kept a specific covenant child alive for a specific appointed work. And behind all of them, giving the pattern its full meaning, stands the Lamb who did not have a substitute because He was the Substitute. Yahusha (Jesus) at Calvary is the final inversion of the pattern. No child dies in His place, because He has become the child for every child. The covenant seed is preserved all through history by the blood of substitutes, and the final substitute becomes the one who preserves the covenant for every seed that will ever believe. The cave in which Abram hid for ten years is worth one more word. Jasher says Yahuah (the Lord) was with Abram in the cave. Every later cave in scripture repeats this promise. Elijah in the cave on Horeb when he thought he was the last faithful in Yashar'el (Israel), and Yahuah (the Lord) came to him in a still small voice (1 Kings 19:9–13). David in the caves of Adullam, writing psalms that would outlast the cave by three thousand years (Psalm 57, Psalm 142). The Maccabean martyrs and the Hebrews 11 faithful wandering in caves and dens of the earth (Hebrews 11:38). The early saints of Acts gathering in catacombs when Rome had banned the Name. The awakening remnant in our own day, hidden in plain sight, whom the systems of the four houses have not yet seen. Every cave has the same Visitor. "Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy presence from the pride of man: thou shalt keep them secretly in a pavilion from the strife of tongues" (Psalm 31:20). Whatever cave the Father has placed you in, He is in it with you. The coming out happens in His timing. Until then, the cave is not a punishment. The cave is a provision. Cross-references: Matthew 2:1–18; Revelation 12:1–6, 13–17; Exodus 1:22–2:10; 1 Kings 19:9; Hebrews 11:37–38; Psalm 27:5 (“he shall hide me in his pavilion… in the secret of his tabernacle shall he hide me”); Isaiah 49:2 (“in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me”); Genesis 15:1; Exodus 1:22–2:10; 2 Kings 11:1–3; 2 Chronicles 22:10–12; Matthew 2:13–18; Revelation 12:1–17; 1 Kings 19:9–13; Psalm 31:20; Psalm 57:1; Psalm 142:1–7; Hebrews 11:37–38.

chapters.title: Abram Reasons Out Elohim, and the Tower of Babel

verses.text: And Haran, the son of Terah, Abram’s oldest brother, took a wife in those days.
Haran was thirty-nine years old when he took her; and the wife of Haran conceived and bare a son, and he called his name Lot.
And she conceived again and bare a daughter, and she called her name Milca; and she again conceived and bare a daughter, and she called her name Sarai.

Haran was forty-two years old when he begat Sarai, which was in the tenth year of the life of Abram; and in those days Abram and his mother and nurse went out from the cave, as the king and his subjects had forgotten the affair of Abram.

And when Abram came out from the cave, he went to Noah and his son Shem, and he remained with them to learn the instruction of YAHUAH (the Lord) and his ways, and no man knew where Abram was, and Abram served Noah and Shem his son for a long time.

And Abram was in Noah’s house thirty-nine years, and Abram knew YAHUAH from three years old, and he went in the ways of YAHUAH until the day of his death, as Noah and his son Shem had taught him; and all the sons of the earth in those days greatly transgressed against YAHUAH, and they rebelled against him and they served other gods, and they forgot YAHUAH who had created them in the earth; and the inhabitants of the earth made to themselves, at that time, every man his god; gods of wood and stone which could neither speak, hear, nor deliver, and the sons of men served them and they became their gods.

And the king and all his servants, and Terah with all his household were then the first of those that served gods of wood and stone. 20 8. And Terah had twelve gods of large size, made of wood and stone, after the twelve months of the year, and he served each one monthly, and every month Terah would bring his meat offering and drink offering to his gods; thus did Terah all the days. 9. And all that generation were wicked in the sight of YAHUAH, and they thus made every man his god, but they forsook YAHUAH who had created them. 10. And there was not a man found in those days in the whole earth, who knew YAHUAH (for they served each man his own Elohim (God)) except Noah and his household, and all those who were under his counsel knew YAHUAH in those days. 11. And Abram the son of Terah was waxing great in those days in the house of Noah, and no man knew it, and YAHUAH was with him. 12. And YAHUAH gave Abram an understanding heart, and he knew all the works of that generation were vain, and that all their gods were vain and were of no avail. 13. And Abram saw the sun shining upon the earth, and Abram said to himself Surely now this sun that shines upon the earth is Elohim, and him will I serve. 14. And Abram served the sun in that day and he prayed to him, and when evening came the sun set as usual, and Abram said within himself, Surely this cannot be Elohim? 15. And Abram still continued to speak within himself, Who is he who made the heavens and the earth? who created upon earth? where is he? 16. And night darkened over him, and he lifted up his eyes toward the west, north, south, and east, and he saw that the sun had vanished from the earth, and the day became dark. 17. And Abram saw the stars and moon before him, and he said, Surely this is the Elohim who created the whole earth as well as man, and behold these his servants are gods around him: and Abram served the moon and prayed to it all that night. 18. And in the morning when it was light and the sun shone upon the earth as usual, Abram saw all the things that YAHUAH Elohim (the Lord God) had made upon earth. 19. And Abram said to himself Surely these are not gods that made the earth and all mankind, but these are the servants of Elohim, and Abram remained in the house of Noah and there knew YAHUAH and his ways’ and he served YAHUAH all the days of his life, and all that generation forgot YAHUAH, and served other gods of wood and stone, and rebelled all their days. 20. And king Nimrod reigned securely, and all the earth was under his control, and all the earth was of one tongue and words of union. 21. And all the princes of Nimrod and his great men took counsel together; Phut, Mitzraim, Cush and Canaan with their families, and they said to each other, Come let us build ourselves a city and in it a strong tower, and its top reaching heaven, and we will make ourselves famed, so that we may reign upon the whole world, in order that the evil of our enemies may cease from us, that we may reign mightily over them, and that we may not become scattered over the earth on account of their wars. 22. And they all went before the king, and they told the king these words, and the king agreed with them in this affair, and he did so. 23. And all the families assembled consisting of about six hundred thousand men, and they went to seek an extensive piece of ground to build the city and the tower, and they sought in the whole earth and they found none like one valley at the east of the land of Shinar, about two days’ walk, and they journeyed there and they dwelt there. 24. And they began to make bricks and burn fires to build the city and the tower that they had imagined to complete. 25. And the building of the tower was to them a transgression and a sin, and they began to build it, and whilst they were building against YAHUAH Elohim of heaven, they imagined in their hearts to war against him and to ascend into heaven. 26. And all these people and all the families divided themselves in three parts; the first said We will ascend into heaven and fight against him; the second said, We will ascend to heaven and place our own gods there and serve them; and the third part said, We will ascend to heaven and smite him with bows and spears; and Elohim knew all their works and all their evil thoughts, and he saw the city and the tower which they were building. 27. And when they were building they built themselves a great city and a very high and strong tower; and on account of its height the mortar and bricks did not reach the builders in their ascent to it, until those who went up had completed a full year, and after that, they reached to the builders and gave them the mortar and the bricks; thus was it done daily. 28. And behold these ascended and others descended the whole day; and if a brick should fall from their hands and get broken, they would all weep over it, and if a man fell and died, none of them would look at him. 29. And YAHUAH knew their thoughts, and it came to pass when they were building they cast the arrows toward the heavens, and all the arrows fell upon them filled with blood, and when they saw them they said to each other, Surely we have slain all those that are in heaven. 30. For this was from YAHUAH in order to cause them to err, and in order; to destroy them from off the face of the ground. 31. And they built the tower and the city, and they did this thing daily until many days and years were elapsed. 32. And Elohim said to the seventy angels who stood foremost before him, to those who were near to him, saying, Come let us descend and confuse their tongues, that one man shall not understand the language of his neighbor, and they did so to them. 33. And from that day following, they forgot each man his neighbor’s tongue, and they could not understand to speak in one tongue, and when the builder took from the hands of his neighbor lime or stone which he did not order, the builder would cast it away and throw it upon his neighbor, that he would die. 34. And they did so many days, and they killed many of them in this manner. 35. And YAHUAH smote the three divisions that were there, and he punished them according to their works and designs; those who said, We will ascend to heaven and serve our gods, became like apes and elephants; and those who said, We will smite the heaven with arrows, YAHUAH killed them, one man through the hand of his neighbor; and the third division of those who said, We will ascend to heaven and fight against him, YAHUAH scattered them throughout the earth. 36. And those who were left amongst them, when they knew and understood the evil which was coming upon them, they forsook the building, and they also became scattered upon the face of the whole earth. 37. And they ceased building the city and the tower; therefore he called that place Babel, for there YAHUAH confounded the Language of the whole earth; behold it was at the east of the land of Shinar. 38. And as to the tower which the sons of men built, the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up one third part of it, and a fire also descended from heaven and burned another third, and the other third is left to this day, and it is of that part which was aloft, and its circumference is three days’ walk. 39. And many of the sons of men died in that tower, a people without number. « • • • Jasher 9:13–19 is one of the most famous passages in all of Jewish tradition about Abram — the young man in Noah’s household who, observing the sun and the moon, reasons his way out of idolatry and toward the Creator. This passage has been preserved in midrash and folklore for millennia. Jasher gives it to us in its earliest written form. And what it tells us is beautiful and load-bearing. Abram did not have the written Torah. He did not have a prophet standing over him with an open scroll. He had the heavens. And by looking at the heavens, he worked out that whatever made the sun and the moon was not the sun or the moon themselves. The sun sets. The moon waxes and wanes. The Maker of the sun does not set. Paul will later make exactly this argument in Romans 1:20 — “the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made.” Paul was not inventing that argument. He was quoting the experience of Abraham. This is how the father of the faithful came to faith. He watched the heavens and refused to worship anything less than what had made them. This is a rebuke, both to the atheist who stares at creation and sees nothing, and to the pagan who stares at creation and worships the thing instead of the Maker. Abram represents the third option — the awakened man who sees through creation to the One who made it. This is why we are told in Genesis 26:5 that Abraham “obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” Nobody gave him a copy of the Torah. He received the Torah the same way creation itself received it — built in, before Sinai, before Moses, before even the patriarchs were named. Torah is older than the stars. The stars keep it. Abram looked at them and worked back from them and found its Author. And then Jasher chapter 9 takes us to Babel. Verse 26 is one of the most chilling verses in Jasher. The people of Babel did not simply want to build a monument. They divided themselves into three divisions of explicit hostility: one group to ascend to heaven and fight YAHUAH; one group to ascend and put their own gods there; one group to ascend and shoot YAHUAH with arrows. This is not architecture. This is an organized assault on the throne of heaven by created men who had lost their fear. The tower is a weapon. The city is a staging ground. The builders are a militia. This is the blueprint of every anti-YAHUAH system that has ever arisen. Every one of them — from Babel to Rome to the modernist academy to the technocratic singularity — divides along these same three lines. Fight Him (militant atheism, active rebellion, Nietzschean “death of God”). Replace Him (syncretism, self-deification, new age “ascension,” every religion that elevates man to the throne). Shoot Him (blasphemy, mockery, the cultural assault on His name). These three strategies have been running for four thousand years. They all lose. Jasher tells us what YAHUAH did: He turned their arrows back onto themselves (verse 29), He confused their tongues so they could not coordinate (verse 32), and He scattered them across the earth (verse 35). The anti-YAHUAH coalition fails every time, and every time the fracture is linguistic. The lesson is: the moment an anti-YAHUAH coalition achieves a unified tongue, YAHUAH splits the tongue. That is worth sitting with in our moment. Every attempt at a unified global consciousness — whether by empire or by economy or by religion or by machine — runs into the same divine boundary. Every attempt to rebuild Babel ends the same way Babel did. And notice in verse 32: “Elohim said to the seventy angels who stood foremost before him, to those who were near to him, saying, Come let us descend and confuse their tongues.” Seventy angels. Deuteronomy 32:8 in the earliest manuscripts reads that YAHUAH divided mankind “according to the number of the sons of Elohim” — seventy nations assigned to seventy heavenly supervisors. Jasher 9:32 confirms that tradition. Every nation has a heavenly overseer (compare Daniel 10:13, 20 — the prince of Persia, the prince of Greece). This is part of the prophetic frame of the whole Tanakh. The gods of the nations are real beings; they are lesser beings; they were once delegated authorities who rebelled and began to be worshiped as gods. Psalm 82 pronounces judgment on them. The scattered seed is still, in a sense, living inside the territories of those fallen delegates. The final gathering includes the judgment of those gods. Babel's three-faction assault as the root of Daniel's four beasts Jasher 9:26 is a verse most readers race past because the arithmetic feels strange — the builders of Babel divided themselves into three factions rather than the one we expect. Slow down at this verse. This is the taxonomy of anti-covenant rebellion, and Daniel 7's four beasts are that taxonomy re-deployed in four successive imperial forms. Read Jasher 9 carefully enough and the whole prophetic arc from Babel to Revelation unfolds in its right order. Jasher says the first faction of Babel wanted to ascend to heaven and fight Yahuah (God). The second faction wanted to ascend to heaven, place their own gods there, and serve them. The third faction wanted to ascend to heaven and shoot Yahuah (God) with bows and spears. Three strategies, one enemy, one assault. Label them plainly: fight Him, replace Him, shoot Him. Every anti-covenant kingdom from Babel forward has operated on some combination of these three strategies, and the Daniel 7 vision presents them in four historical costumes over the course of the Times of the Gentiles. Daniel 7 gives us four beasts — a lion with eagle's wings, a bear with three ribs in its mouth, a four-headed leopard, and a fourth dreadful beast with iron teeth and ten horns. Daniel 2 gives us the same empires in a different image — a gold head, a silver chest and arms, a bronze belly and thighs, iron legs, and iron-mixed-with-clay feet. The historical identifications are well established across both Jewish and Christian traditions: Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece, and Rome. What is less often named is that each of these four is a specific costume of the one Nimrodic spirit, deploying a specific one of Babel's three strategies as its primary weapon. "After this I saw in the night visions, and behold a fourth beast, dreadful and terrible, and strong exceedingly; and it had great iron teeth: it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet of it: and it was diverse from all the beasts that were before it; and it had ten horns" (Daniel 7:7). The fourth beast is the composite, the distillation, the summary — the beast from which the ten horns will finally crown the Antichrist-figure of Revelation 13. But the lineage runs back through the three before it, and through each of those to Babel. Babylon under Nebuchadnezzar worked the replace-Him strategy. When Nebuchadnezzar conquered Yahudah (Judah), he carried the vessels of the temple into the house of his gods (Daniel 1:2) — not to destroy them but to absorb them into his own pantheon. He took the sons of the royal line and enrolled them in his own wisdom school (Daniel 1:3–5). His project was to assimilate, to translate, to absorb. Daniel 3's golden image is the whole thing compressed into one monument — a statue before which every nation, every tongue, every people would bow. Replace-Him. Put our own gods on the throne of heaven and worship them. Babel's second faction rebuilt in Babylonian iconography. Medo-Persia, the silver chest and bear, worked the legislate-around-Him strategy. Darius did not denounce the Elohim (God) of Daniel; he let himself be manipulated by his satraps into signing a decree that for thirty days no petition could be made to any Elohim (God) or man except the king (Daniel 6:7). The rebellion was administrative. The system of law itself was bent into a tool that excluded the Most High from the territory of daily petition. Daniel prayed anyway. The lion's mouth was shut. The decree failed. But the strategy is preserved in the record — administrative law as the anti-covenant weapon. Every regime since that has outlawed prayer in schools, crosses on public buildings, Sabbath observance in workplaces, and Torah in the common square is operating on the Medo-Persian playbook. Legislate-around-Him. This is fight-Him in its bureaucratic form — Babel's first faction wearing the robes of a lawful court. Greece, the bronze belly and leopard, worked the replace-Him strategy with philosophical precision. Where Babylon was crude — a statue on a plain — Greece was sophisticated. Hellenism did not ban the Most High. Hellenism subsumed Him. The Septuagint became a battleground. The gymnasium came to Jerusalem (1 Maccabees 1:14). The high priesthood was sold. The temple was rededicated to Olympian Zeus by Antiochus IV Epiphanes in 167 BCE. The Greek project was not to destroy the covenant seed but to Hellenize it, to translate it, to reinterpret every word of Tanakh through a philosophical grid until the covenant itself had been re-voiced in the grammar of the Academy. Replace-Him with Plato. Replace-Him with Aristotle. Replace-Him with a philosophical abstraction that has the same syllables but none of the same weight. The institutional church would later carry this project forward with devastating success, dressing the Hebrew Messiah (Christ) in Greek metaphysics and calling the result theology. Nicaea and Chalcedon and the whole creedal apparatus are downstream of Greek grammar imposed on a Hebrew covenant. This is why Yoshi's voice does not use Nicene vocabulary even when defending the divinity of Yahusha (Jesus): the vocabulary itself is a Hellenistic reconstruction. The Christology of the prophets is the Christology of the prophets — the Formed of the Formless, the Ancient of Days walking in the flesh, the Son in whom the fullness of the Formless dwells bodily. The Father is not a member of a pantheon. He is the Formless from whom the Formed proceeds. Greek grammar cannot say that without adding errors it was not designed to avoid. Greek was the replace-Him language of Babel's second faction, refined over centuries into a system so elegant that centuries of believers have mistaken it for the faith itself. Rome, the iron legs and dreadful ten-horned beast, worked the shoot-Him strategy. Rome did not translate the covenant or absorb the gods. Rome fed the saints to lions. Rome crucified. Rome beheaded. Rome built the Colosseum on the model of the Circus Maximus and turned public entertainment into a devotional act of blood against the seed of promise. The seventy years of persecution after Nero, the intermittent purges under Decius and Valerian and Diocletian, the ritualized executions, the demand for the pinch of incense before the emperor's image — Rome's project was to make the confession of the Name itself illegal. Arrows and spears against heaven. Babel's third faction in legionary armor. Each beast worked primarily one strategy while drawing on the other two at need. Each beast had its season. Each beast fell to the next. And the fourth beast — "diverse from all the beasts that were before it" (Daniel 7:7) — did not simply represent historical Rome. It pointed forward to the composite end-beast of Revelation 13, in which all three strategies converge in one final regime. "And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion" (Revelation 13:2). Greek leopard, Medo-Persian bear, Babylonian lion — and the iron teeth of Rome holding them together. Every strategy Babel invented is deployed simultaneously at the end. Replace-Him through a global religious synthesis. Legislate-around-Him through a mark of the beast that governs commerce and access. Shoot-Him through the martyrdom of every saint who will not take the mark. The end-beast is Babel rebuilt with every strategy fully weaponized. Notice what Yahuah (God) did at Babel and what He does at every recurrence. "Come, let us descend and confuse their tongues, that one man shall not understand the language of his neighbor" (Jasher 9:32; compare Genesis 11:7). The fracture mechanism is linguistic. The moment an anti-covenant coalition achieves a unified tongue, the Father splits the tongue. Babylon fell when its language of imperial religion could no longer hold the provinces. Medo-Persia fell when its legal-administrative lingua franca cracked under the weight of its own decrees. Greece fell when Hellenization's philosophical tongue could no longer bind an empire Alexander's successors had carved into four. Rome fell when Latin could no longer enforce a unified Christendom, and what scattered it into the vernaculars was, providentially, the translation of the Word into the languages of the people. Every Babel ends the same way. Every coalition against the Most High finds its tongue confused at the moment the tower is nearly complete. This pattern means something for the awakening reader of this generation. Every attempt at a unified global consciousness — whether by empire or by economy or by technology or by religion or by a technological neural integration that promises to unify human cognition — is operating on Babel's blueprint. Every attempt to rebuild the tower ends at the fracture of the tongue. The present age is tower-building at scale. The Father's answer will be the same answer He has given since Jasher 9. He will not be mocked (Galatians 6:7). The confusion of the tongue is sovereign. What man unifies in rebellion, the Father scatters in mercy — because a unified Babel is a Babel that can complete the tower, and the Father has never let the tower be completed. And none of this is grounds for despair. The Father has never been frightened by any Babel. He descended on Hermon when the Watchers swore. He descended on Babel when the tower rose. He descended in the Messiah (Christ) at Bethlehem when the ancient promise had been delayed four thousand years. He will descend in the revealing of Yahusha (Jesus) when the last tower approaches its completion. The beast is not a surprise to heaven. The beast is the last iteration of a pattern the Father has always known how to fracture. The awakening remnant is not preparing for a battle Yahuah (God) might lose. The remnant is preparing to witness the fall of the fourth beast exactly as it witnessed the fall of the first. Cross-references: Genesis 11:1–9; Romans 1:18–23; Deuteronomy 32:8–9; Psalm 82:1–8; Daniel 10:13, 20; Acts 17:26–28; Genesis 26:5; Isaiah 40:26; Revelation 17:1–18; Acts 14:15–17; Daniel 2:31–45; Daniel 7:1–28; Daniel 3:1–30; Daniel 6:1–28; Daniel 1:1–5; Revelation 13:1–18; 1 Maccabees 1:14–15, 54–59; Galatians 6:7; 2 Thessalonians 2:3–12; Revelation 17:1–18; Genesis 11:5–9.

chapters.title: The Scattering — The Nations Seeded, and Where the Seed

verses.text: And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.

And when YAHUAH (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.
And all the families became each according to its language, its land, or its city.
And the sons of men built many cities according to their families, in all the places where they went, and throughout the earth where YAHUAH had scattered them.

And some of them built cities in places from which they were afterward extirpated, and they called these cities after their own names, or the names of their children, or after their particular occurrences.

And the sons of Japheth the son of Noah went and built themselves cities in the places where they were scattered, and they called all their cities after their names, and the sons of Japheth were divided upon the face of the earth into many divisions and languages.
And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.
And the children of Gomer, according to their cities, were the Francum, who dwell in the land of Franza, by the river Franza, by the river Senah.
And the children of Rephath are the Bartonim, who dwell in the land of Bartonia by the river Ledah, which empties its waters in the great sea Gihon, that is, oceanus.

And the children of Tugarma are ten families, and these are their names: Buzar, Parzunac, Balgar, Elicanum, Ragbib, Tarki, Bid, Zebuc, Ongal and Tilmaz; all these spread and rested in the north and built themselves cities.
And they called their cities after their own names, those are they who abide by the rivers Hithlah and Italac to this day.
But the families of Angoli, Balgar and Parzunac, they dwell by the great river Dubnee; and the names of their cities are also according to their own names.

And the children of Javan are the Javanim who dwell in the land of Makdonia, and the children of Medaiare are the Orelum that dwell in the land of Curson, and the children of Tubal are those that dwell in the land of Tuskanah by the river Pashiah.

And the children of Meshech are the Shibashni and the children of Tiras are Rushash, Cushni, and Ongolis; all these went and built themselves cities; those are the cities that are situate by the sea Jabus by the river Cura, which empties itself in the river Tragan.

And the children of Elishah are the Almanim, and they also went and built themselves cities; those are the cities situate between the mountains of Job and Shibathmo; and of them were the people of Lumbardi who dwell opposite the mountains of Job and Shibathmo, and they conquered the land of Italia and remained there to this day.
And the children of Chittim are the Romim who dwell in the valley of Canopia by the river Tibreu.
And the children of Dudonim are those who dwell in the cities of the sea Gihon, in the land of Bordna.

These are the families of the children of Japheth according to their cities and languages, when they were scattered after the tower, and they called their cities after their names and occurrences; and these are the names of all their cities according to their families, which they built in those days after the tower.
And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.
All these went and built themselves cities as they found fit places for them, and they called their cities after the names of their fathers Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan.
And the children of Mitzraim are the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuchim, Pathrusim, Casluchim and Caphturim, seven families.
All these dwell by the river Sihor, that is the brook of Egypt, and they built themselves cities and called them after their own names.

And the children of Pathros and Casloch intermarried together, and from them went forth the Pelishtim, the Azathim, and the Gerarim, the Githim and the Ekronim, in all five families; these also built themselves cities, and they called their cities after the names of their fathers to this day.
And the children of Canaan also built themselves cities, and they called their cities after their names, eleven cities and others without number.
And four men from the family of Ham went to the land of the plain; these are the names of the four men, Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboyim.
And these men built themselves four cities in the land of the plain, and they called the names of their cities after their own names.
And they and their children and all belonging to them dwelt in those cities, and they were fruitful and multiplied greatly and dwelt peaceably.

And Seir the son of Hur, son of Hivi, son of Canaan, went and found a valley opposite to Mount Paran, and he built a city there, and he and his seven sons and his household dwelt there, and he called the city which he built Seir, according to his name; that is the land of Seir to this day.
These are the families of the children of Ham, according to their languages and cities, when they were scattered to their countries after the tower.

And some of the children of Shem son of Noah, father of all the children of Eber, also went and built themselves cities in the places wherein they were scattered, and they called their cities after their names.
And the sons of Shem were Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram, and they built themselves cities and called the names of all their cities after their names.

And Ashur son of Shem and his children and household went forth at that time, a very large body of them, and they went to a distant land that they found, and they met with a very extensive valley in the land that they went to, and they built themselves four cities, and they called them after their own names and occurrences.
And these are the names of the cities which the children of Ashur built, Ninevah, Resen, Calach and Rehobother; and the children of Ashur dwell there to this day.
And the children of Aram also went and built themselves a city, and they called the name of the city Uz after their eldest brother, and they dwell in it; that is the land of Uz to this day.

And in the second year after the tower a man from the house of Ashur, whose name was Bela, went from the land of Ninevah to sojourn with his household wherever he could find a place; and they came until opposite the cities of the plain against Sodom, and they dwelt there.
And the man rose up and built there a small city, and called its name Bela, after his name; that is the land of Zoar to this day.
And these are the families of the children of Shem according to their language and cities, after they were scattered upon the earth after the tower.
And every kingdom, city, and family of the families of the children of Noah built themselves many cities after this.

And they established governments in all their cities, in order to be regulated by their orders; so did all the families of the children of Noah forever. « • • • Jasher chapter 10 is the expanded Table of Nations, and it is worth spending time on for one reason only: this is where the prophetic map of the scattered seed begins. The nations listed here — Francum in France, Bartonim, Tugarma (Togarmah), Lumbardi in Italy, Romim (Rome) — correspond to the lands where the House of Israel would later be scattered. Ezekiel 38–39 names Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal; Jasher 10 tells us who Gomer and Magog and Tubal are and where they went. The prophetic geography of the end of days is already being written in Jasher 10. The scattered seed of Israel — the ten tribes taken by Assyria in 722 BC, the two tribes taken by Babylon in 586 BC, the dispersion by Rome in 70 AD — did not go into empty territory. They went into lands that had been settled by the sons of Noah for 1,500 years before Israel was a nation. YAHUAH planted the nations first, and then planted His covenant seed among them. When the scattering came, Israel was scattered into lands already named in the Table of Nations. Every Englishman and Frenchman and German in the modern world is descended from sons of Japheth by blood — and also carries, in many cases, the bloodlines of the scattered tribes that were salted into those Japhethite nations by the Assyrian and Roman dispersions. This is the Two-House understanding in embryo. This is why Yahusha (Jesus) could say in Matthew 15:24 that He was sent “to the lost sheep of the house of Israel” and then commission His disciples in Matthew 28:19 to go to “all nations.” The two statements are not in contradiction. The lost sheep are in the nations. You find the sheep by going to the nations. This is also why the inclusion-gospel reading is wrong. The claim that anyone who believes and Torah-keeps is thereby counted as Israel collapses the distinction between the scattered seed and the nations around them. The prophets named a real people. That people went into real lands. That people are going to be regathered out of real lands — and the Gentile nations are going to accompany them home (Isaiah 14:1–2; Zechariah 8:23). The regathering of Israel is not the elimination of the Gentiles. It is the regathering of the specific people to whom the covenant was made, along with a company of righteous nations who cleaved to them. Jasher 10 is the seedbed for all of that. The nations had to be named before the nations could be redeemed. And notice the understated line in verse 11: “Those are they who abide by the rivers Hithlah and Italac to this day.” Jasher was written (in its final form) at a time when these distributions could still be traced. The compiler knew where the descendants of Tugarma were living. The ethnographic memory of the Tanakh is not mythical. It is rooted in real populations. The prophetic calendar of Ezekiel, Daniel, Zechariah, and Revelation presupposes that these populations are real and traceable and that YAHUAH is dealing with them as distinct actors in the last days. The geography of the gathering One more architectural note before we leave the scattering. Jasher 10's ethnographic detail — that the descendants of Tugarma dwell in a certain land, that the descendants of Chittim dwell by the Tibreu, that the Francum are at the river Franza — is preserved in the text because Yahuah's (God's) dealings with the scattered seed are not abstract. They run in specific territories. The prophetic geography of the last days requires specific peoples in specific places, and Jasher preserves the map under names many modern readers no longer recognize. Consider a short test of the architecture. Ezekiel 38 names Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, as the leader of a coalition coming against the regathered house of Yashar'el (Israel) in the latter days. Gog, Magog, Meshech, and Tubal are Japhethite names from Jasher 10. The coalition Ezekiel describes is drawn from the northern territories the sons of Japheth settled. The land they come against is the land Yahuah (God) gave to Abraham's seed forever (Jasher 13:7). The battle Ezekiel prophesies presupposes that both parties — the coalition and the covenant people — are still real, still traceable, and still located in the geography Jasher named. If the Table of Nations is a legend rather than a map, Ezekiel 38 is a rhetorical flourish without a stage to happen on. If the Table of Nations is preserved ethnographic memory, Ezekiel 38 is a specific prophecy whose specific players are already on their specific boards. The same test applies to the gathering. Isaiah 11:11 names Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea as the territories from which the second recovery will come. Every one of those regions is named in Jasher 7–10. The scattered seed is being drawn out of specific places and brought back to a specific land. This operation is not a metaphor for spiritual awakening in general. It is a sovereign regathering of a named people from named territories, which requires — and therefore proves — the geography Jasher preserved. The nations among whom the seed was scattered are not merely neutral ground. They are inheritances under named overseers who were delegated authority at Babel and who have in most cases fallen into the worship Psalm 82 condemns. This is why the prophetic canon speaks of judgment on nations as the regathering unfolds. Joel 3:2 names the valley of Jehoshaphat as the place of judgment: "I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Yashar'el (Israel), whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land." The nations that scattered Yashar'el (Israel), that took its land, that absorbed its exiles without honoring the covenant — these are brought to account. Not randomly. By name. The Father kept the names. And for the awakening reader whose ancestry runs somewhere in those Japhethite lines — whose grandfather was English, whose great-grandmother was Italian, whose family has been in Germany or France or Ireland or Denmark or Poland as far back as memory reaches — the question is not whether the reader's blood is worthy. The question is whether the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) was salted into that particular stream at some point in the twenty-seven centuries since 722 BCE. For many in the awakening remnant, the answer is yes. For others, the answer is no. The Father knows the answer in each case, and the walk of Torah and the hearing of the Shepherd's voice is the same walk either way. The seed is called home by name by the Shepherd. The nation that walks alongside is blessed in its station. Both roads are good roads. Neither road is walked by a self-declaration of identity. The Father's call does the identifying. The awakening reader who is certain of nothing about lineage is invited, in this commentary as in all of Yoshi's work, to walk the walk and leave the accounting to the Father. What He has planted, He will not mis-sort in the harvest. What was scattered among the nations by exile is not lost from Him. What was born of the nations and adopted into the covenant household by grafting or by sojourn is not diminished in the household. The Shepherd knows every sheep. The Father knows every name. The awakening is not an enrollment office. It is a coming home to a Father who already knew you were His. Cross-references: Genesis 10:1–32; Deuteronomy 32:8–9; Ezekiel 38:1–39:29; Isaiah 66:18–21; Matthew 15:24; Matthew 28:19; Zechariah 8:20–23; Isaiah 14:1–2; Isaiah 49:22–23; Jeremiah 31:10; Ezekiel 38:1–23; Ezekiel 39:1–29; Joel 3:1–21; Isaiah 11:11–16; Jeremiah 23:7–8; Jeremiah 16:14–16; Romans 11:1–5.

chapters.title: Abram Smashes the Idols

verses.text: And Nimrod son of Cush was still in the land of Shinar, and he reigned over it and dwelt there, and he built cities in the land of Shinar.
And these are the names of the four cities which he built, and he called their names after the occurrences that happened to them in the building of the tower.

And he called the first Babel, saying, Because YAHUAH (the Lord) there confounded the language of the whole earth; and the name of the second he called Erech, because from there Elohim (God) dispersed them.

And the third he called Eched, saying there was a great battle at that place; and the fourth he called Calnah, because his princes and mighty men were consumed there, and they vexed YAHUAH, they rebelled and transgressed against him.
And when Nimrod had built these cities in the land of Shinar, he placed in them the remainder of his people, his princes and his mighty men that were left in his kingdom.

And Nimrod dwelt in Babel, and he there renewed his reign over the rest of his subjects, and he reigned securely, and the subjects and princes of Nimrod called his name Amraphel, saying that at the tower his princes and men fell through his means.

And notwithstanding this, Nimrod did not return to YAHUAH, and he continued in wickedness and teaching wickedness to the sons of men; and Mardon, his son, was worse than his father, and continued to add to the abominations of his father.
And he caused the sons of men to sin, therefore it is said, From the wicked goes forth wickedness.
At that time there was war between the families of the children of Ham, as they were dwelling in the cities which they had built.

And Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, went away from the families of the children of Ham, and he fought with them and he subdued them, and he went to the five cities of the plain and he fought against them and he subdued them, and they were under his control.
And they served him twelve years, and they gave him a yearly tax.
At that time died Nahor, son of Serug, in the forty-ninth year of the life of Abram son of Terah.
And in the fiftieth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, Abram came forth from the house of Noah, and went to his father’s house.
And Abram knew YAHUAH, and he went in his ways and instructions, and YAHUAH his Elohim (the Lord his God) was with him.
And Terah his father was in those days, still captain of the host of king Nimrod, and he still followed strange gods.
And Abram came to his father’s house and saw twelve gods standing there in their temples, and the anger of Abram was kindled when he saw these images in his father’s house.
And Abram said, As YAHUAH lives these images shall not remain in my father’s house; so shall YAHUAH who created me do to me if in three days’ time I do not break them all.

And Abram went from them, and his anger burned within him. And Abram hastened and went from the chamber to his father’s outer court, and he found his father sitting in the court, and all his servants with him, and Abram came and sat before him.

And Abram asked his father, saying, Father, tell me where is Elohim who created heaven and earth, and all the sons of men upon earth, and who created you and me. And Terah answered his son Abram and said, Behold those who created us are all with us in the house.

And Abram said to his father, My Lord, shew them to me I pray you; and Terah brought Abram into the chamber of the inner court, and Abram saw, and behold the whole room was full of gods of wood and stone, twelve great images and others less than they without number.
And Terah said to his son, Behold these are they which made all you see upon earth, and which created me and you, and all mankind.
And Terah bowed down to his gods, and he then went away from them, and Abram, his son, went away with him.
And when Abram had gone from them he went to his mother and sat before her, and he said to his mother, Behold, my father has shown me those who made heaven and earth, and all the sons of men.

Now, therefore, hasten and fetch a kid from the flock, and make of it savory meat, that I may bring it to my father’s gods as an offering for them to eat; perhaps I may thereby become acceptable to them.

And his mother did so, and she fetched a kid, and made savory meat of it, and brought it to Abram, and Abram took the savory meat from his mother and brought it before his father’s gods, and he drew nigh to them that they might eat; and Terah his father, did not know of it.
And Abram saw on the day when he was sitting amongst them, that they had no voice, no hearing, no motion, and not one of them could stretch forth his hand to eat.

And Abram mocked them, and said, Surely the savory meat that I prepared has not pleased them, or perhaps it was too little for them, and for that reason they would not eat; therefore tomorrow I will prepare fresh savory meat, better and more plentiful than this, in order that I may see the result.

And it was on the next day that Abram directed his mother concerning the savory meat, and his mother rose and fetched three fine kids from the flock, and she made of them some excellent savory meat, such as her son was fond of, and she gave it to her son Abram; and Terah his father did not know of it.

And Abram took the savory meat from his mother, and brought it before his father’s gods into the chamber; and he came nigh to them that they might eat, and he placed it before them, and Abram sat before them all day, thinking perhaps they might eat.
And Abram viewed them, and behold they had neither voice nor hearing, nor did one of them stretch forth his hand to the meat to eat.
And in the evening of that day in that house Abram was clothed with the spirit of Elohim.

And he called out and said, Wo to my father and this wicked generation, whose hearts are all inclined to vanity, who serve these idols of wood and stone which can neither eat, smell, hear nor speak, who have mouths without speech, eyes without sight, ears without hearing, hands without feeling, and legs which cannot move; like them are those that made them and that trust in them.
And when Abram saw all these things his anger was kindled against his father, and he hastened and took a hatchet in his hand, and came to the chamber of the gods, and he broke all his father’s gods.

And when he had done breaking the images, he placed the hatchet in the hand of the great god which was there before them, and he went out; and Terah his father came home, for he had heard at the door the sound of the striking of the hatchet; so Terah came into the house to know what this was about.
And Terah, having heard the noise of the hatchet in the room of images, ran to the room to the images, and he met Abram going out.

And Terah entered the room and found all the idols fallen down and broken, and the hatchet in the hand of the largest, which was not broken, and the savory meat which Abram his son had made was still before them.
And when Terah saw this his anger was greatly kindled, and he hastened and went from the room to Abram.
And he found Abram his son still sitting in the house; and he said to him, What is this work you have done to my gods?

And Abram answered Terah his father and he said, Not so my Lord, for I brought savory meat before them, and when I came nigh to them with the meat that they might eat, they all at once stretched forth their hands to eat before the great one had put forth his hand to eat.

And the large one saw their works that they did before him, and his anger was violently kindled against them, and he went and took the hatchet that was in the house and came to them and broke them all, and behold the hatchet is yet in his hand as you see.
And Terah’s anger was kindled against his son Abram, when he spoke this; and Terah said to Abram his son in his anger, What is this tale that you have told? You speak lies to me.

Is there in these gods spirit, soul or power to do all you have told me? Are they not wood and stone, and have I not myself made them, and can you speak such lies, saying that the large god that was with them smote them? It is you that did place the hatchet in his hands, and then say he smote them all.

And Abram answered his father and said to him, And how can you then serve these idols in whom there is no power to do any thing? Can those idols in which you trust deliver you? can they hear your prayers when you call upon them? can they deliver you from the hands of your enemies, or will they fight your battles for you against your enemies, that you should serve wood and stone which can neither speak nor hear?

And now surely it is not good for you nor for the sons of men that are connected with you, to do these things; are you so silly, so foolish or so short of understanding that you will serve wood and stone, and do after this manner?
And forget YAHUAH Elohim (the Lord God) who made heaven and earth, and who created you in the earth, and thereby bring a great evil upon your souls in this matter by serving stone and wood?
Did not our fathers in days of old sin in this matter, and YAHUAH Elohim of the universe brought the waters of the flood upon them and destroyed the whole earth?

And how can you continue to do this and serve gods of wood and stone, who cannot hear, or speak, or deliver you from oppression, thereby bringing down the anger of the Elohim of the universe upon you?
Now therefore my father refrain from this, and bring not evil upon your soul and the souls of your household.
And Abram hastened and sprang from before his father, and took the hatchet from his father’s largest idol, with which Abram broke it and ran away.

And Terah, seeing all that Abram had done, hastened to go from his house, and he went to the king and he came before Nimrod and stood before him, and he bowed down to the king; and the king said, What dost you want?

And he said, I beseech you my Lord, to hear me–Now fifty years back a child was born to me, and thus has he done to my gods and thus has he spoken; and now therefore, my Lord and king, send for him that he may come before you, and judge him according to the law, that we may be delivered from his evil.

And the king sent three men of his servants, and they went and brought Abram before the king. And Nimrod and all his princes and servants were that day sitting before him, and Terah sat also before them.

And the king said to Abram, What is this that you have done to your father and to his gods? And Abram answered the king in the words that he spoke to his father, and he said, The large god that was with them in the house did to them what you have heard.

And the king said to Abram, Had they power to speak and eat and do as you have said? And Abram answered the king, saying, And if there be no power in them why dost you serve them and cause the sons of men to err through your follies?

Dost you imagine that they can deliver you or do anything small or great, that you should serve them? And why will you not sense the Elohim of the whole universe, who created you and in whose power it is to kill and keep alive?
0 foolish, simple, and ignorant king, woe to you forever.
I thought you would teach your servants the upright way, but you have not done this, but have filled the whole earth with your sins and the sins of your people who have followed your ways.
